articles.title: Work with Action Center actions

sections.text: An action is one piece of work with an outcome, built from the evidence behind it. GetCito groups many signals into one action: six valuable pages with no AI traffic become one "Capture AI traffic" action with six linked signals, not six rows. New actions are added after the daily tracking run, on the **Actions** tab.

sections.heading: Action categories
sections.text:
- **Growth**: ground you could win, such as demand, topics, platforms or pages where you could appear more.
- **Protect**: ground you hold that is starting to slip.
- **Recover**: ground you held and lost, in visibility, citations, mentions or traffic.
- **Fix**: issues on your own site, such as low audit scores, blocked crawlers or broken links AI sends people to.
- **Compete**: places where competitors lead you.

sections.heading: Cards and filters
sections.text:
The cards at the top count and filter the list, all but **Highest Priority**. Click one to narrow the table, and click it again to clear it.

- **Top Actions**: the five highest-priority open actions.
- **At Risk**: open Recover and Fix actions.
- **Opportunities**: open Growth actions.
- **In Progress**: actions someone is working on.
- **Highest Priority**: the highest level among open actions; it doesn't filter. While Getting started runs, its card shows instead.

Below them, filter by category, **Priority**, **Status** (including **Stale**) and **Assignee**, or search. **Sort** by Priority (the default), Newest, Due date or Recently updated. Filters are kept in the page's address, so a filtered view can be shared. For an online shop, the **From Products** chip lists only the actions sent from Products.

sections.heading: Status, dismiss and delete
sections.text:
An action's status is **New**, **In Progress**, **On Hold**, **Completed** or **Dismissed**. The row menu sets In Progress, Completed or Dismiss without opening the action.

Dismissing asks why: it doesn't matter to us, it's already done, the data behind it is wrong, or not now. You can also dismiss without saying why. History shows the reason.

**Delete**, for admins and managers only, removes an action for everyone, and it won't come back on its own the next day.

sections.heading: Stale actions
sections.text:
An action that has stayed **New** for 30 days, with no one assigning, editing, sending or updating its tasks, is marked **Stale** each night. It isn't closed or dismissed: it shows a **Stale** label next to its status, and the **Status** filter's **Stale** lists them all.

If it still matters, click **Still relevant** in the open action, or in the row menu. The label goes, its 30 days start again, and History says who kept it. Any other change to the action, or moving it out of New, clears the label too. If it no longer matters, dismiss it.

sections.heading: Inside an action
sections.text:
Click a row to open the action. Under its title you set **Status**, **Assignee** and **Due date**. Its tabs:

- **Overview**: **Why this priority?**, with how sure the score is (low, medium or high confidence, and why, such as one kind of finding from one source), **Why this action?** with the signals behind it, the **Goal** (what done looks like, with a date) and the linked **KPIs**.
- **Affected**: the prompts, pages, topics, competitors or platforms it is about, with each prompt's demand.
- **Tasks**: the work, step by step.
- **Signals**: the evidence. Click one to open it on the Signals tab.
- **History**: every change, from status and assignee changes to tasks updated or sent.

sections.heading: Run an agent on an action
sections.text:
When Chat is on, Admins and Managers see **Run agent** on each open action: an agent button next to its title in the list, and at the top of the open action.

It lists your agents that work on the action's brand, the ones used on this kind of action first. Pick one, and Chat starts a run on this action alone and opens it beside the action. **Run with Chat** does the same without an agent, in your default mode. **Create an agent for this kind of action** starts a new agent from a fitting skill.

The run drafts the work, but closing tasks stays your click. If the action is completed or dismissed, an agent's run stops; a **Run with Chat** run doesn't. The action's **History** shows when a run started and ended, and who started it.

sections.heading: Assign work
sections.text: An action with no one on it belongs to **Everyone** in the workspace until someone takes it. Pick a teammate in the action's **Assignee** field, and set a **Due date** if it has one. The **Assignee** filter on the Actions tab shows one person's actions, or **Everyone** for the unassigned ones.

sections.heading: Export actions
sections.text:
**Export CSV** on the Actions tab downloads the actions in the current view, as filtered, with their priority, status, assignee, due date, task progress and affected items.

Inside an action, **Copy Data** gives the whole action as Markdown to paste into a doc or ticket, and **Export** downloads it as **Export CSV** or **Export Excel**. The Excel file has one sheet each for the action, its affected items, tasks, signals and history.

sections.heading: Send work here from other pages
sections.text:
Most actions come from signals each night, but you can also send work to the Action Center:

- **Mentions**: select answers, or open one, and click **Send to Action Center**.
- **Content**: **Send to Actions** on a content opportunity, or **Assign to…** on a Content Plan row.
- **New content**: send it to a teammate with **Send to Action Center**.
- **Site Audit**: **Send to Action Center** on a page's audit report.
- **AI Referral Traffic**: select pages and click **Send to Action Center**.
- **Brand Visibility**: **Send action** on a topic in Opportunities.
- **Product Visibility**: pick the work in a product's plan and click **Send … actions to Action Center**.
- **Prompts**: **Send Actions** on a prompt's Improve tab.
- **Chat**: **Send to Action Center** under an answer. Its Overview links back to the chat.

Sending the same thing twice doesn't create a second action: the page says it is already in the Action Center.

articles.title: Track KPIs in the Action Center

sections.text: The **KPIs** tab tracks the goals you set for the brand. Each KPI shows its **Value**, **Change**, **Trend (7D)**, **Goal**, progress **vs Goal** and a **Status**. An action's Overview lists the KPIs it is linked to.

sections.heading: KPIs you can track
sections.text:
AI Visibility, Citations, Mentions, Share of Voice, AI Referral Traffic and Positive Sentiment.

A brand that never had KPIs starts with a suggested set: AI Visibility, Citations, Mentions, Share of Voice and Positive Sentiment, plus AI Referral Traffic when Google Analytics is connected. Each aims 20% above its last 30 days, or starts from a default where there's no data yet. It is saved the first time an admin or manager opens the tab.

sections.heading: KPI status
sections.text:
- **Goal Reached**: 100% of the goal or more.
- **On Track**: 70% or more, and not moving the wrong way.
- **At Risk**: 40 to 69%, or moving the wrong way before the goal is reached.
- **Off Track**: under 40%.

sections.heading: Change your KPIs
sections.text: Click **Edit KPIs** (or **Configure KPIs**) to open the framework. Pick a template (**AI Search Visibility**, **Brand Monitoring** or **Custom Framework**; **Content Performance** is marked coming soon), a time period (Weekly, Monthly or Quarterly) and a target for each KPI, then click **Save & Apply**. Only admins and managers can change KPIs.

articles.title: Action Center overview

sections.text: The **Action Center** is where GetCito turns what changed in AI search into a ranked list of work. It is the first page you see after you sign in. Everything in it is per brand: switch brands to see another brand's work.

sections.heading: The tabs
sections.text:
- **Actions**: what to do now, ranked by Priority Score.
- **Signals**: what changed across your AI visibility data.
- **KPIs**: the goals you track for the brand.
- **History**: what was done, and what it moved.

Admins and managers also see **Needs review**, where tasks the AI wrote without some of their details wait for a person.

sections.heading: How the work flows
sections.text: Signals are detected after your daily tracking run. GetCito groups related signals into one action, so a long list of findings becomes a few pieces of work. At most five new actions are added per brand per day, so the list stays short enough to act on. Each action comes with tasks. When you close an action as **Completed**, History measures what changed afterwards.

sections.heading: While the first tracking runs
sections.text: While a new brand's first tracking runs, one thin line sits under the tabs: **First tracking running**, how many of its checks are done and about how long is left. If another analysis is running, the line says **First tracking queued** until a slot opens. Click **Details** to read what it means and follow the run on Brand Visibility. Actions, signals and KPIs fill in once it finishes, and the line goes away. Meanwhile, a new brand starts with the **Getting started** steps on the Actions tab.

sections.heading: A weekly routine
sections.text: Work from the **Top Actions** card each week. Assign each action, set a due date, and close it as **Completed** when its tasks are done, so History can measure the result.

articles.title: Signals in the Action Center

sections.text: The **Signals** tab lists what changed: a visibility drop, a lost citation, a competitor gaining, a page with no AI traffic, a site issue. Signals are detected after your daily tracking runs, and they are the evidence actions are built from. Many of the same changes also appear in the Daily Pulse email.

sections.heading: Cards and filters
sections.text:
The cards show Total, Important (high impact), New and Resolved signals, and the average signal impact, for the selected range (7, 30 or 90 days) against the range before.

Filter by category (Visibility, Citation, Mention, Traffic, Technical, Competitor), **Impact**, **Status**, **Source** (AI Results, Google Analytics, Google Search Console, Site Audit) and **Platform**, or search.

sections.heading: Signal status
sections.text: A signal is **New**, **Acknowledged**, **Resolved** or **Dismissed**. Set it from the row menu, and use **Reopen** to bring one back. When you resolve or dismiss a signal, the actions it supports get their Priority Score again right away.

sections.heading: Inside a signal
AI traffic signals
sections.text:
The nightly pass also watches AI Referral Traffic and raises these signals:

- **AI visits fell from … to … week over week**: AI visits over the last 7 whole days fell 40% or more from the 7 before, which had at least 30. It feeds **Recover AI traffic**.
- **Broken AI links on …**: in the last 7 days, AI visitors landed on a missing page that AI answers cite, or three or more landed on another missing page. It feeds **Fix broken citation targets**.
- **AI search bots haven't read … that AI answers cite**: needs 30 days of AI-bot data. It feeds **Fix AI crawler accessibility**.
- **… started sending visitors**: an AI platform sent visits for the first time.

articles.title: Action history and results

sections.text: The **History** tab lists actions once they are In Progress, On Hold, Completed or Dismissed, with what they were meant to do and what has been measured since. A result is measured after the action, not proven to be caused by it.

sections.heading: Find an action in History
sections.text:
Filter by range (7d, 30d, 90d, All), **Status**, **Type**, **Priority** and **Source**, and sort by Newest, Oldest or Priority. The cards count total, completed, in-progress, no-improvement and dismissed actions in the window.

Click an action to see **What was the goal?**, **What happened?** (the signals it was built from), its affected items and tasks, and its **Result**.

sections.heading: How a result is measured
sections.text:
Only a completed action is measured. Its metrics are read three times, over the week ending 7, 14 and 30 days after it closed, each against the 7 days before it was raised. Until the final reading on day 30, the result reads *so far*, and the drawer lists each reading.

An action that names its prompts or pages is measured on them, with the brand-wide figures beside. Its prompts' change is also shown net of the brand's prompts it didn't touch, so a change that hit every prompt, such as an engine's update, is told apart from its own. A Site Audit fix is judged by its pages audited again since it closed.

sections.heading: What a result means
sections.text:
- **Improved**, **Mixed**, **No meaningful change** or **Declined**: judged by the action's main metric, the first one it names. **Mixed** means another metric it names moved the other way.
- **Not measured**: the action was dismissed.
- **Not measurable**: it has no metric to read, or its main metric is mentions or citations and tracking missed more than two nights in one of its weeks.

The drawer also says what became of the signals that raised it: how many ended, turned into another, were dismissed, or are still open.

sections.heading: Actions sent from Improve
sections.text: An action sent from a prompt's Improve tab reports on how many platforms its position improved. It is read again daily while the action is open, and for 30 days after it is completed.

sections.heading: The Scorecard
sections.text: Switch History from **Actions** to **Scorecard** to see what each kind of action did at this brand over the range, 90 days unless you pick another. It shows how many were completed, their results so far, the **Success rate** (the share of results that improved, shown once a kind has three), the median change in each action's main metric, and how many were dismissed, with the reason given most often. It counts this brand's own actions only.

sections.heading: When a problem comes back
sections.text: When an action is closed, its condition can open a new action after a two-week rest if it is still firing. The old one stays in History as the record of that round of work.

articles.title: Action Priority Score

sections.text: Every action has a **Priority Score** from 0 to 100: how soon to work on it beside the others. Impact says how much an action could matter; priority weighs impact together with the evidence behind it. The score sets the default order of the **Actions** tab and the **Top Actions** card.

sections.heading: Priority levels
sections.text:
- **Critical**: 90 and above.
- **High**: 75 to 89.
- **Medium**: 50 to 74.
- **Low**: below 50.

sections.heading: What goes into the score
sections.text:
- **Impact**: the action's impact grade, high, medium or low.
- **Demand**: how much its prompts, search queries or pages are searched or visited. Only the most demanded few count. A prompt's measured demand level raises it: High more, Medium a little.
- **Severity**: a loss ranks above a sharp drop, a drop above a slip, and a slip above a gap or a site issue.
- **Business value**: how commercial the searches are, or what a page is worth from Google Analytics.
- **Confidence**: how many independent kinds of finding and data sources agree.
- **Recoverability**: ground you held and lost is nearer at hand than ground you never held.
- **Recency**: newer evidence counts more.

Demand or business value that nothing measures neither raises nor lowers the score.

sections.heading: Past success
sections.text: On top of these, past success nudges the score: how this brand's own earlier actions of the same kind turned out over the last six months, as the History scorecard counts them. A kind that improved results here sits up to 10 points higher, one that rarely did up to 10 lower. A few results barely move it, and a kind with no results yet doesn't move at all. Other brands' results are never used.

sections.heading: When the score changes
sections.text:
An action is scored when it is created, and again every night from that night's evidence. When you resolve or dismiss a signal, the actions it supports are scored again right away. An action not scored yet shows a dash and sorts after the scored ones.

An action sent from another page has no detection signals, so it is scored from what it carries, such as the prompts or pages that were sent.

sections.heading: Why this priority?
sections.text: The action's **Overview** tab starts with **Why this priority?**: one sentence written from the facts the score rests on. It says what changed, on what, how recently, and what makes it matter. When past success moves the score by a point or more, it says so too.

sections.heading: Not the Content Plan's score
sections.text: The Content Plan has its own Priority Score, which ranks the Plan's pages. The two are worked out separately.

articles.title: Action tasks and how they are checked

sections.text: Each action comes with tasks: concrete steps such as "Refresh content for these prompts" or "Add structured data to these pages". You find them on the action's **Tasks** tab.

sections.heading: What a task tells you
How we check
sections.text:
**How we check** says how a task is confirmed:

- **Automatic**: GetCito fetches the page again.
- **Re-run**: the prompts run again.
- **Manual**: you confirm it.

Automatic checks run every night, and when you click **Check now**. Only pages on the brand's own site are read. A task that passes is completed by itself, and History says so. One that doesn't shows **Last check** with what is still missing. Site Audit fixes are checked by your next audit.

sections.heading: What an automatic check looks for
sections.text:
- **A broken page**: the page answers again.
- **Publishing**: the page answers where it wasn't before.
- **Structured data**: the audit checks that raised the action now pass on the page.
- **Crawler access**: robots.txt lets the AI crawlers in, and the page isn't noindex.
- **Optimizing or refreshing**: the page changed by more than a date, a price or a rotating quote. Blocks that change by themselves, such as the latest posts, don't count.
- **New text**: the task's new text is on the page, and the text it replaces is gone.

A task you reopen after it passed stays open: the call is yours.

sections.heading: Task status
sections.text: A task's status is **To Do**, **In Progress**, **Completed**, **Skipped** (with a reason), **Waiting Approval**, or **Failed** when GetCito couldn't carry it out itself and it needs doing by hand. Skipped tasks leave the count, so they don't hold an action short of done. Use **Add task** for work of your own, and delete tasks you don't need.

sections.heading: Hand a task on
sections.text:
From a task you can:

- **Create content** or **Optimize page**: open a draft in the Content Editor for this task. **Open draft** returns to it, and marking the draft ready completes the task.
- **Send to Content**: send a content task to Content as an opportunity, where a brief can be written for it.
- **Send to webhook**: post the task to the brand's webhook, for a workflow outside GetCito. Set it up under **Content › Webhook Settings** with the **Action Center task sent** event selected.

sections.heading: Files attached from Chat
sections.text:
When Chat attaches a file or a draft to a task, the task's details list it under **Attached from Chat**: its name, who attached it, when, and **Open**. A draft opens in the Content Editor; any other file downloads. A paperclip with a count shows on the task row.

Each attachment is also a line in the action's **History**, as is a task Chat set to **Ready for review**. Neither changes the task's status: you mark it done yourself.

sections.heading: Regenerate tasks
sections.text:
Where AI task writing is on for your workspace, **Regenerate tasks** writes the action's tasks again from its evidence, in your brand's terms, by the **Site type** in the brand settings. Done, under-way and hand-added tasks stay. It uses your plan's monthly AI allowance.

The AI also reads this brand's last three closed rounds of the same action. It builds on what improved results here, and doesn't hand out again a task that was done without effect. A task it writes without its URL, Change, Done when or How we check waits on **Needs review**.

sections.heading: Tasks GetCito does itself
sections.text: Some tasks that only read data, such as checking a page's traffic in your connected Analytics, can be carried out by GetCito overnight. The action's History says so. Nothing that would change something outside GetCito runs without your approval: such a task waits as **Waiting Approval**.

sections.heading: Comparing pages overnight
sections.text:
Two tasks compare pages for you overnight:

- **Compare competitor content and coverage** reads up to three pages AI answers cited for the action's prompts, your competitors' first, and your own cited page. It says which checks at least half of their pages pass that yours doesn't.
- **Find what sets your winning pages apart** compares up to three of your winning pages with your other pages that Site Audit checked. It lists what most winning pages have and the others lack, and the pages missing the most of it.

When there is nothing to compare, the task stays open with the reason, and GetCito tries again a week later.

articles.title: Getting started steps in the Action Center

sections.text: A new brand starts with **Getting started**: a fixed list of 17 steps on the Action Center's **Actions** tab. While it runs, the **Getting started** category opens first and lists the steps with their **Stage**, **Status** and **Ready** time, and a **Getting started** card shows how many are done. Click **All** or another category to see your actions.

sections.heading: The four stages
sections.text:
- **Set up**, ready now: set your KPIs, add at least 3 competitors and 3 topics, add 3 prompts per topic, connect Google Search Console and Google Analytics, and add the AI Traffic snippet.
- **Explore**, when the first AI answers are in (usually within an hour): see where you stand in Brand Visibility, read your first AI answers, track high-value prompt suggestions, check what AI says about you, see who AI quotes and see visits from AI.
- **Act**, when the first content suggestions are in (about 24 hours): pick content from suggestions, create your first content, optimize a page.
- **Ready**, after every step above is done or skipped.

The high-value prompts step waits about 24 hours after you connect Search Console or Analytics.

sections.heading: Complete a step
sections.text: Click a step to open its card: why it matters, how to do it, and when it counts as done. The card's button opens the step's page in a new tab. Most steps are checked automatically from your data, such as three competitors saved or a first AI visit detected, so the step updates when you come back to the Action Center tab. A step still waiting for its data says when it opens.

sections.heading: While the first tracking runs
sections.text: A new brand's first tracking takes from a few minutes to an hour or two at busy times. Meanwhile, the steps you can do right away come first and carry a **Ready now** mark: KPIs, competitors, topics and prompts you haven't finished, Google Search Console, Google Analytics and the AI Traffic snippet. The steps that need the first answers say **Arriving now**. Their card shows how far tracking is, such as "Your first answers are arriving (18 of 40) · ~6 min", instead of a page that is still empty. When tracking finishes, the app says **Your first results are ready**, the list goes back to its usual order and those steps open.

sections.heading: Skip the Google steps
sections.text: **Connect Google Search Console** and **Connect Google Analytics** are optional. Admins and managers can **Skip** them. A skipped step counts as complete, and you can still connect later from Settings. Without either one, prompt and content suggestions are less accurate.

sections.heading: Start or skip Getting started
sections.text:
Admins and managers see **Get Started** or **Skip Get Started** at the top right of the Actions tab.

- **Skip Get Started** puts the actions list back to normal. Steps you finished stay done, and you can start again any time from the same button.
- **Get Started** appears after a skip, and for an existing brand whose setup looks incomplete: fewer than 3 competitors or topics, no Search Console, or no content in the last 30 days.
- A brand added to an organization that already has one asks first whether to run Getting started for it. Choose **Run Getting started** or **Skip**.

sections.heading: Steps are not actions
sections.text: Getting started steps are not actions: they have no Priority Score and never come from signals. Your actions are listed beside them, under **All** and the other categories.

articles.title: Review tasks waiting in Needs review

sections.text: A task the AI writes without its **URL**, its **Change**, **Done when** or **How we check** doesn't reach the action's task list. It waits on the Action Center's **Needs review** tab instead, with what it misses. Only admins and managers see the tab and review tasks.

sections.heading: Approve a task
sections.text: Click **Edit**, fill the missing fields and click **Approve**. The task is added after the action's other tasks. All four fields, the URL, the change, Done when and How we check, must be filled before it can be approved.

sections.heading: Dismiss a task
sections.text: Click **Dismiss** on a task you don't want. A dismissed task never reaches its action.

sections.heading: Where these tasks come from
sections.text: They come from AI task writing, such as **Regenerate tasks** on an action. Only the tasks that miss one of the four fields wait here; the others go straight to the action's **Tasks** tab. Tasks of an action that is completed, dismissed or deleted aren't listed.

articles.title: See which AI bots read your site

sections.text: The **AI bots reading your site** section of **AI Traffic Analytics** shows which AI bots read your pages, from your own Cloudflare or Vercel. Only verified bots count: the bot's name and its operator's published addresses must both match. Today that's the bots of OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity.

sections.heading: What the section shows
sections.text:
- **By bot type**: hits, pages read and last seen for **Training**, **Search index** and **User fetch**, with the bots under each.
- **Pages AI bots read**: hits per page, and when each type last read it.
- **The search-bot alert**: pages AI answers cited in the last 30 days that no AI search bot read in that time. It starts 30 days after the first AI-bot request, and pauses when the bot data doesn't cover the last 30 days or the month's cap was reached.

sections.heading: Connect AI bots
sections.text:
Click **Connect** on the **AI bots** card in the Data sources strip, and choose how your site sends AI-bot requests: **Cloudflare Worker** (recommended), **Cloudflare Logpush** or **Vercel Drain** (Vercel Pro and Enterprise only). Each option says what it costs on your own Cloudflare or Vercel bill before you connect, and none of them changes your site's speed.

Click **Create connection** and follow the numbered steps. Copy the settings right away: the secret in them isn't shown again. If you lose it, revoke the connection and create a new one.

sections.heading: Manage connections
sections.text: **Manage** on the card lists your connections with their last request, lets you **Revoke** one, and shows this month's use. Plans in cloud mode store a monthly number of detailed rows; past it, detailed rows pause until the next month and the totals are still counted. Cloudflare Logpush and Vercel Drain also have a monthly number of log records; past it, they aren't read until the next month. Only requests to your brand's own domains, or their subdomains, are kept.

sections.heading: Dates and sample data
sections.text:
Bot counts are kept by UTC day, so the 24-hour range reads yesterday and today (UTC), and All time reads the last 90 days.

On the Starter plan, the section shows sample data with **Upgrade**. Without a connection, it offers **Connect** or **Preview with sample data**.

articles.title: AI Referral Traffic page

sections.text: **AI Referral Traffic** in the sidebar opens the **AI Traffic Analytics** page. It measures real visits to your site from AI assistants, what those visits are worth, and whether AI is changing your Google traffic. Most analytics tools count these visits as direct or referral traffic; GetCito tells each assistant apart.

sections.heading: Date range and changes
sections.text:
Pick a range: 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, All or Custom. The page opens on the last 24 hours, then on the range you last picked in this browser, and every section follows it.

Each figure is compared with the period of the same length just before. Below 30 visits in either period, the change reads **Low sample** instead of a percentage. A platform or page with no visits before reads **new**. All time has no previous period.

sections.heading: How visits are counted
sections.text:
- **One visit per session**: a reload, or a further link from the same answer, continues the visit. The visits card gives the pageviews beside the visits.
- **Snippet or Google Analytics, never both**: on days the tracking snippet sent any visit, the page counts the snippet's; on other days, Google Analytics'. The visits card says how many days came from Google Analytics.
- **Recent AI Referral Visits**, at the bottom, shows only the snippet's visits, one row per visit. Search it by address and filter by platform.
- **No snippet, no zero**: until the tracking snippet is seen on your site, the page says **Tracking code not detected** and how to add it, rather than showing 0 visits. Chat and the MCP tools say the same.

sections.heading: Summary line and cards
Trend and platforms
sections.text:
- **AI Referral Trend**: **By platform** shows visits per day, or per hour on 24h. **vs Google clicks** sets AI visits beside Google clicks; it needs Search Console and a range of 7 days or longer. On **vs Google clicks**, dashed lines mark the days actions entered the Action Center or prompts were added.
- **Platform Breakdown**: each AI platform's share of visits.
- **Referrals by Platform**: visits and change per platform, with **Engaged** and **Key events** from Google Analytics.
- **Top Landing Pages**: the pages with the most AI visits, and how often tracked answers cite them.

AI Overviews and AI Mode clicks are part of Google organic clicks, and Google doesn't let them be separated.

sections.heading: Where AI visitors convert
sections.text:
With Google Analytics connected, two tables show what AI visits bring:

- **Top converting pages from AI**: landing pages ranked by key events from AI visits, or by revenue when the property reports it, with the best platform.
- **Which answers bring buyers**: the topics of your tracked prompts whose answers cite those converting pages, by AI platform.

A range with fewer than 30 AI visits uses the last 30 days here, and says so.

sections.heading: Which AI assistants count
sections.text: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Grok, DeepSeek, Meta AI, You.com, Phind, Poe and Google Labs. The snippet also counts Bing's Copilot answer links, as **Bing**. A visit counts when it comes from one of their sites, or from a link tagged with their name. Google Analytics' own **AI Assistant** channel also shows assistants that aren't on the list yet. AI visits that arrive with neither count as Direct. Visits from ChatGPT Shopping product cards show as **ChatGPT Shopping**; they're part of ChatGPT's visits.

sections.heading: Export the page
sections.text: **Export** gives the whole page as **Excel (.xlsx)**, one sheet per section, or **CSV (.zip)**, one file per section. Each table also has its own Excel and CSV buttons. A range with more than 100,000 visits is too large to export at once.

sections.heading: Weekly AI Traffic e-mail
sections.text:
Every Monday, an e-mail about the week before goes to each brand's Daily Pulse recipients, if the brand had AI visits that week or the one before. It shows AI visits with the change, the top platform, the summary line, visits by day and platform, and the top changes.

To turn it off for a brand, untick **AI Traffic weekly digest** in **Settings › Notifications**; admins and managers can change it. It isn't sent while the brand's Daily Pulse is **Off**. The e-mail is in cloud mode only.

articles.title: AI traffic by page and Google query

sections.text: The **Pages** section of **AI Traffic Analytics** answers which pages get AI visits, which don't, and why. Below it, the Google Search Console tables show whether AI is changing your Google traffic.

sections.heading: The Pages tabs
sections.text:
- **No AI traffic**: pages with traffic in Google Analytics or in your sitemap that got no AI visit, most valuable first. **AI visibility** says why: **Cited**, **Not cited** or **No prompt**.
- **Cited, not clicked**: pages AI answers cited at least 20 times in the range that got no AI visit.
- **Traffic, no prompt**: pages AI assistants sent visitors to that no tracked prompt's answer cited.
- **Broken AI links**: pages AI visitors landed on that don't exist.
- **All pages**: every page with AI visits, citations, traffic or a sitemap entry in the range.

sections.heading: Next steps from a page
sections.text:
Rows carry their next step: **Audit page** for a page AI cites or a prompt targets, **Add prompts** for one no prompt points to.

On **No AI traffic** and **Cited, not clicked**, each row's **…** menu also has **Send to Action Center**, **Add prompts** and **Suggest content**. Under the list, **Audit N cited pages** (or **Audit N pages**) starts Site Audits for the pages shown, and **Send to Action Center** sends them as one action. Only admins and managers can add prompts or suggest content.

sections.heading: Add prompts for a page
sections.text: **Add prompts** suggests questions people ask AI assistants that the page answers, including ones from its Search Console queries, and lets you add your own. The prompts you track from it point to the page, so their answers show whether AI cites it. Each one uses a prompt slot on your plan.

sections.heading: Fix broken AI links
sections.text:
**Broken AI links** shows what the visitor got: **Not found (404)**, **Gone (410)**, **Shows a not-found page (200)** for a site that shows its own not-found page, or **Page title says not found** where the browser reports no status.

Each comes with a suggested **Redirect to**: a **Similar page**, **The page above it** or the **Home page**. Addresses with a query string get no suggestion. With the tab open, the Excel and CSV buttons export the redirect list. Add the tracking snippet to your 404 page too, so these visits are seen.

sections.heading: Is AI taking Google clicks?
sections.text: With Search Console connected, **Is AI taking Google clicks?** lists pages whose impressions rose 15% or more while their click-through rate fell 20% or more, among pages with at least 100 impressions in the period before. An AI Overview may be answering in place of the click. **Positions** shows whether you're cited for a tracked prompt about the page; **Add prompts** appears when none is about it yet.

sections.heading: Untracked Google queries
sections.text: **Untracked Google queries** lists Search Console queries with clicks that no tracked prompt covers, most clicked first. **Track** adds one as a prompt; **Track all** adds the listed ones that your plan's prompt slots allow. Admins and managers can track queries.

articles.title: Track conversions from AI visits

sections.text: Google Analytics' key events say how many AI sessions converted. To see which pages AI visitors went through on the way to a signup, a demo form or an order, turn on conversions for the brand. The snippet then follows visitors who came from an AI assistant for 30 days, and credits each conversion to the assistant that first sent them.

sections.heading: Turn conversions on
sections.text:
In **Brand Settings › Tracking**, under **Conversions from AI visits**, tick **Track conversions from AI visits** and choose **Consent**:

- **Wait for the visitor's consent** (recommended): no journey is followed until your site says the visitor agreed. AI visits themselves are counted as before.
- **Don't wait: our own banner covers it**: only if your cookie banner already asks for analytics storage, or where no consent is needed.

Conversions are off by default, and only admins and managers can change them.

sections.heading: Replace the tag
sections.text:
Under **Use this tag**, copy the tag with the copy button on its code, and use it in place of the one you have, on every page. The tag carries your choices, so after you change **Consent**, copy it again.

To turn conversions off, untick **Track conversions from AI visits** and put the tag without them back.

sections.heading: Tell GetCito when a visitor agrees
sections.text:
With **Wait for the visitor's consent**, your cookie banner has to tell the snippet when the visitor agrees, and when they say no or take consent back. Google Consent Mode needs nothing more. A banner set up inside Google Tag Manager needs a tag there for agreeing and one for refusing.

The visitor has to agree on the page the AI assistant sent them to: agreeing on a later page doesn't bring the journey back.

sections.heading: What counts as a conversion
sections.text:
- A form with an email field counts as a signup on its own, once per page load. Contact and newsletter forms count too, unless you give them their own goal. Login forms don't count, and nothing typed in a form is sent.
- Anything else, such as a thank-you page or a purchase, needs a conversion call from your site's own code.
- On Shopify, orders come from a Customer events pixel. Copy it under **Shopify store** in **Brand Settings › Tracking** and add it in Shopify admin as a custom pixel.

sections.heading: Where you see the results
sections.text: The Content Editor shows what came of it: the **Live page** tab for each page, and the **From AI visits** line on the Content **Plan** for the whole site.

sections.heading: What it can't see
sections.text:
- Visitors who refuse cookies, or who agree only after leaving the page the AI assistant sent them to.
- AI visits that arrive without a referrer: they count as Direct.
- Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode.
- Journeys from one subdomain to another.
- Forms inside an embedded widget, forms sent from a script, and posts without a form. These need a conversion call from your site's code.
- Conversions after the browser has cleared the visitor's id, as Safari can after about a week without a visit to your site.

articles.title: Connect AI traffic data sources

sections.text: The **Data sources** strip at the top of **AI Traffic Analytics** shows the four sources the page reads, and each one's state. A section whose source isn't connected stays on the page with a **Needs …** tag and a **Connect …** button for that source. Only admins and managers can connect a source.

sections.heading: What each source adds
sections.text:
- **Tracking snippet**: AI-referred visits, page by page, as they happen.
- **Google Analytics**: AI visits on days the snippet has none, plus engaged visits, key events, revenue and the AI share of all traffic.
- **Google Search Console**: Google clicks, the pages where AI may be taking them, and the Google queries you don't track yet.
- **AI bots**: which AI bots read your pages, from your own Cloudflare or Vercel, on the Growth plan and above.

sections.heading: Add the tracking snippet
sections.text:
Until the snippet is seen on your site, the page opens with **Tracking code not detected on** your domain, the steps to add it and the snippet itself. **Install** in the Data sources strip opens it too; once the snippet is seen, the button reads **Code**. The page fills in your own address and tracking code, so copy it rather than typing it.

Add it to the head of every page you want to track, your 404 page included, so **Broken AI links** can see visitors who land on a missing page.

sections.heading: Check that the snippet works
What the snippet collects
sections.text:
The snippet sends nothing for a visitor who didn't come from an AI assistant. For an AI-referred visit it sends the page address, the referrer, the AI source, the browser, its language and screen size, and the page's status as the browser saw it. GetCito adds the country.

The snippet sets no cookies, and without conversions it stores nothing in the visitor's browser. The visitor's IP address is never stored.

sections.heading: Connect Google Analytics and Search Console
sections.text:
Click **Connect** on either card in the Data sources strip and sign in to Google; access is read-only. If the card then reads **Connected · choose a property for this brand**, pick the property under **Manage**, in **Settings › Integrations**. Connections are shared across your organization.

On a self-hosted server, both cards read **Not set up on this server** until the server has its Google connection keys.

sections.heading: When the first numbers arrive
sections.text: Google Analytics' first numbers arrive in about 15 minutes; up to 14 months of history can take up to 24 hours. Search Console's can take up to 48 hours, because Google reports about two days late.

articles.title: See and run your agents in Agent Center

sections.text: An agent is a saved skill, mode, connections and model that runs in Chat again and again: on a schedule, when Action Center finds a signal, when a KPI changes, or when someone clicks **Run now**. **Agent Center** offers ready-to-use agents and lists every agent you can see, and each agent has its own page with its triggers, its runs and how much of your monthly AI limit it uses.

sections.heading: Open Agent Center
sections.text:
Click **Agent Center** on the left menu, right under **Chat**. It has a page of its own, outside Chat. It is also in the chat menu, under **Inbox**, where it shows **New** until you first open Agent Center. You can also press Ctrl K (⌘K on a Mac) in Chat and type "Agent Center". Old links to Agents in Chat open Agent Center.

It has two tabs: **Ready to use**, which opens first, and **Your agents**. In **Your agents**, the filters above the list show how many agents each holds:

- **Mine**: the agents you own.
- **Workspace**: the agents shared with everyone in your workspace. Admins also see their teammates' private agents here.
- **Paused** and **Archived**: agents that are off.

Type in **Search by name or skill** to find an agent by its name or by a skill it uses.

sections.heading: Ready-to-use agents
sections.text:
**Ready to use** shows agents set up for common jobs, such as **Visibility Watch**, **Citation Win-back** and **Weekly Report**, and agents made for a kind of site or a team, such as **Product Answer Pages** for e-commerce or **CEO Brief** for founders. Each card says what the agent does, its skills, what starts it and its mode. Filter them by **Goal**, **Business type** and **For your role**.

Admins and Managers click **Use this agent**. **New agent** opens with its skills, triggers, mode and connections filled in, for the brand you have open. Change what you like, then click **Save as draft** or **Turn on**. Nothing turns on by itself.

If your plan doesn't include an agent's mode, its card says which plan does, and the agent opens on **Auto, ask before changes**. Cards marked **Soon** say what they're waiting for and can't be used yet.

sections.heading: Agents for your site and your work
sections.text: Agents made for the site type of the brand you have open are marked **For your site type**, and agents made for one of your work areas **For your role**. They come first among the agents you can use, and first among the **Soon** ones. A brand's site type is **E-commerce**, **B2B SaaS** or **B2C**, under **Site type** in the brand's settings; until someone sets it, GetCito guesses it. Change your work areas in **Settings › Account › Your work areas**. **Mobile app** agents show under **Business type** only: a brand can't be set to Mobile app yet.

sections.heading: What each card shows
sections.text:
In **Your agents**, each agent has a card with:

- A dot and its state: green for **Active**, amber for **Paused** with the reason, grey for **Draft** and **Archived**.
- Its skills, its mode and the person who owns it.
- **Trigger**: what starts it, for example "Every Mon 09:00 · New Recover signal", and **Next run**.
- **Scope**: the brand it works on, or how many brands.
- **Last run** with its state, and **Outcomes · 30 days**.
- **AI use · 30 days**: its share of your monthly AI limit, with a thin bar. Hover over it to see its runs, the average share a run and its cap a run.

Usage is always shown as a share of your monthly AI limit.

sections.heading: An agent's page
sections.text:
Click **Open** or the agent's name. The top shows its state, its owner, whether it is private or shared, and **This period**: what it used of this month's AI limit, with its monthly cap when one is set. Under it you see its skills, mode, connections and model.

**Triggers** lists what starts it and when it runs next. **Run history** lists its last 50 runs: when each started, its trigger and brand, its result, its outcome and its **AI use**, for example "3.2% of 10%": what the run used and the most one run may use. Filter them with **All**, **Improved**, **Pending** and **Stopped**, and click a run to open its chat.

On the right, **Access**, **Scope** and **AI use** show who owns it, what it may reach and its limits.

sections.heading: Run, pause and archive
sections.text:
Admins and Managers see the buttons they may use:

- **Run now** starts a run for each brand in its scope. A second click within a minute doesn't start another one.
- **Pause** stops its triggers until you click **Resume**. **Activate** turns on a draft.
- Under **⋯**: **Duplicate** makes a copy as a draft. **Archive** turns it off; its triggers stop and runs waiting to start are cancelled. Admins can also **Take over** an agent, so its triggered runs act as them.
- An archived agent has **Restore**, which brings it back paused.

Managers change their own agents and can run agents shared with the workspace. Admins can do this for every agent.

sections.heading: Create an agent
sections.text:
Admins and Managers click **New agent** in **Agent Center**. Four steps open, with a summary of the agent on the right:

1. **Skill**: pick what it does, add up to 2 follow-on skills, and write instructions if you like.
2. **Trigger**: add up to 5, such as **Schedule** or **Signal created**. Each shows its next run or when it fires. **Manual** is always on: **Run now**. Next to **FOR**, pick its brands, and narrow it to platforms, topics, prompt tags or URLs.
3. **Mode & approvals**: how much it may do without asking.
4. **Connections & model**: then its name, **Private** or **Workspace**, and **Max per run**, the most one run may use of your monthly AI limit. Admins can also set a **Monthly cap**.

Click **Save as draft** to keep it off, or **Turn on**. If something needs fixing, its step opens and says what to change.

sections.heading: Skills an agent can use
sections.text: Step 1 lists the same skills Chat offers. Besides **Win back lost citations**, **Weekly report** and the other content and reporting skills, there are the skills for what you focus on: **Buyer questions**, **How AI compares us**, **No clear leader**, **Who AI recommends by market**, **Listing gaps**, **Rival brief** and **Site audit fixes**. Each card says which connections it uses. These seven work from your GetCito data and public pages, so they need no connection. An agent can run up to 2 follow-on skills after its first one, for example **Comparison page** after **How AI compares us**.

sections.heading: Connections
sections.text:
Step 4 lists the connections the agent's skills use. **Any CMS** counts Webflow, WordPress, Framer, Wix or a workflow webhook. **Any catalog source** counts Merchant Center, a product feed, an upload or a store.

A **Required** connection is one a skill can't work without, such as a CMS for **Ready to publish**. If the brand doesn't have it, the run doesn't start: **Run now** and **Run agent** say which brand lacks it, and an agent that runs on its own pauses with "A required connection is off". **Resume** doesn't turn the agent back on until every brand in its scope has its Required connections: it says which brand lacks which one. An **Optional** one, such as Search Console for **Weekly report**, helps but isn't needed: without it, the agent does everything else and says what it couldn't use.

sections.heading: Edit or delete an agent
sections.text:
On an agent's page, click **Edit** to open the same four steps with its current settings. An agent that is on or paused has **Save changes**; a draft has **Save as draft** and **Turn on**. A change to what it does saves a new version, and a run that already started keeps the version it started with. If someone saved the agent after you opened it, click **Reload** to see their change first.

Managers edit their own agents, and Admins every agent. If your Admin keeps workspace agents to Admins, Managers can't change their agents shared with the workspace either. Analysts and Agency partners see a read-only line with **Ask your Admin** instead.

To delete an agent, archive it first. Then open **⋯** on its page and click **Delete**. Chat asks first; its past runs and files stay.

sections.heading: When an agent runs by itself
sections.text:
A **Schedule** trigger runs at its time on the clock of the time zone it was set in, also when summer time starts or ends. A time missed while the agent was paused isn't made up later. A **Signal** trigger runs when Action Center finds a new signal of its category, and of the definitions, pages and engines you picked. **KPI changed** and **Watch rule** triggers are saved, but don't start runs yet.

Signals that come close together don't each start a run. Signals within 15 minutes join one run, a brand gets at most one signal run every 6 hours, and your plan sets how many signal runs an agent may start a day. A signal that had to wait is listed in the agent's next run, and in **Run history** as **Skipped** with the reason.

sections.heading: How a run works
sections.text:
Each run works on one brand, in a chat of its own. A run a trigger started acts as the agent's owner, with their role; **Run now** acts as the person who clicked it. The chat shows in that person's Inbox.

A run may use only its share of your monthly AI limit. A run a trigger started ends **Stopped at its limit** when it reaches it; a **Run now** run pauses there instead. After 3 failed runs in a row the agent pauses. When the monthly AI limit is used up, the agent pauses and starts again by itself once the limit resets.

sections.heading: When a run asks before a change
sections.text: A **Run now** that starts as you click it follows the agent's mode, so in **Full auto** it makes changes without asking. A run that starts without you, from a trigger or after waiting for a free slot, asks before most changes, whatever its mode. Some still follow the mode, with the role and access of the person the run acts as: creating and changing Content drafts, reviewing or dismissing content opportunities, dismissing prompt suggestions and **Send to Action Center**. In **Full auto** the run makes them without asking; in **Ask me first** it asks. The run reads the agent's mode again before each change. Every change is in the **Activity** log, with **Undo**. When a change needs approval, the run shows **Needs you** and waits. After 7 days without an answer it stops with **No answer in 7 days**.

sections.heading: Let an agent publish on its own
sections.text:
An Admin can let chosen agents send pages to your CMS as drafts without a click. Two switches must be on: **Agents that publish on their own** in **Settings › Chat**, and **Publish and send on its own** on the agent's **Mode & approvals** step, with the agent in **Full auto**. Managers see the box read-only, with **Ask your Admin**.

**At most a day** sets how many pages it may send on its own in 24 hours, from 1 to 20. A page still waits for your click, and its card says why, when it fails Quality or your approved brand facts, the run read text that tried to instruct it, the page has hidden text or outside links, the page is live already, or the agent reached its limit.

Changing what the agent does turns this off until an Admin turns it on again.

sections.heading: Let an agent publish on its own
sections.text:
An Admin can let chosen agents publish new pages on Webflow, WordPress and Wix, and send drafts to your CMS, without a click. Two switches must be on: **Agents that publish on their own** in **Settings › Chat**, and **Publish and send on its own** on the agent's **Mode & approvals** step, with the agent in **Full auto**. Managers see it read-only.

**At most a day** sets how many pages it may send or publish on its own in 24 hours, from 1 to 20. A page still waits for your click, and its card says why, when it fails Quality or your approved brand facts, the run read text that tried to instruct it, the page has hidden text or outside links, the page is live already, or the agent reached its limit.

Changing what the agent does turns this off until an Admin turns it on again.

sections.heading: When an agent sends a page on its own
sections.text:
Its owner and the people it notifies get a notice at the top of their **Inbox**'s **Needs you**, and an e-mail unless their Chat settings say Inbox only: the agent, the page and where it went, with **Open page** (the live page, once published) and **Open run**. A published page's notice also has **Take down**, for Admins and Managers. The notice leaves Needs you once you open it. A page someone took down never goes live on its own again. In the **Content Library**, the page's last send says the agent sent it on its own, and an action the page works on lists it in its History.

When an edit turns it off, the Admin who allowed it and the agent's owner get a notice with **Open agent**, unless they made the edit themselves.

sections.heading: On your own AI key
sections.text: When your workspace runs Chat on its own AI key, agents run on it too. The provider bills your account, and your monthly AI limit doesn't move. **Max per run** and **Monthly cap** still apply: what a run uses is measured at the providers' list prices.

sections.heading: Run an agent from Action Center
sections.text:
Admins and Managers can also start an agent from an open action in Action Center: **Run agent** on the action's row or at the top of the open action lists the agents that work on its brand. The run works on that action alone, acts as the person who clicked, and opens beside the action. Its chat is named after the agent and the action, and **Run history** shows its trigger as **Run agent from an action**.

The run never adds targets to the action and never closes its tasks. If the action is completed or dismissed, the run stops with **The action was closed**. The action's **History** shows **Agent run started** and **Agent run completed**.

sections.heading: Your key's monthly agent limit
sections.text: When your workspace runs on its own AI key, all agents together may spend at most a monthly limit on it: $250 unless an Admin sets another, from $10 to $10,000. It is measured at the providers' list prices, and it can't be turned off. Once agents reach it, each agent pauses when it next runs, with **Key's monthly agent limit reached**, and **Run now** and **Run agent** are refused. They start again by themselves when the month renews, or when an Admin raises the limit in **Settings › AI Providers**. Chats you start yourself don't count toward it.

sections.heading: Read-only roles
sections.text: Analysts and Agency partners see agents but can't create, run or change them. Agency partners see only agents that work on brands shared with them. The list says you see agents read-only, with **Ask your Admin** to send a request. If a button is refused, for example by your role or your plan, Chat shows why, who can do it and what to do next.

sections.heading: When your AI key fails
sections.text:
When your workspace runs on its own AI key and the key fails (the provider turns it down, the account is out of credit, or the key can't reach its model), a run ends **Stopped · AI key not working**. An agent a trigger started pauses with **Your AI key isn't working**. These runs don't count toward 3 failed runs in a row.

While the key fails, Agent Center says so at the top, and **Run now**, **Run agent**, **Turn on** and **Resume** are refused before anything starts. Admins get **Fix in AI Providers**; others read that an Admin can fix it there.

articles.title: Find a chat and see all your chats

sections.text: Chat keeps every chat, so you can find one again by a word in its name or in anything that was said in it. **All chats** lists them all in one place, with your archived chats.

sections.heading: Search chats
sections.text: Type in **Search chats** under **Chats** in the chat menu. The menu then lists the chats whose name or messages have every word you typed, newest first, in place of the days. A few letters are enough: "citat" finds "citations". Click **Clear filters**, or press Esc, to see your chats by day again. Archived chats are left out of the search.

sections.heading: Search from anywhere in Chat
sections.text: Press Ctrl K (⌘K on a Mac) anywhere in Chat to open the search box over the page; press it again to close it. It starts with **New chat** and your latest chats. Type to find chats and Chat pages such as **All chats**. Use the arrow keys and Enter, or click. Enter opens the first match, or starts a new chat when nothing matches. When the chat menu is hidden, the **Search** button at the top opens the same box.

sections.heading: All chats
sections.text: Click **All chats** at the bottom of the chat menu. **Active** lists every chat you can open: yours and the ones teammates shared with you, with the step each one is on, who started it and when it last changed. Search there looks through names and messages too. The filters show only chats that are **Running**, **Needs you** or **Done**, your own (**Mine**), or chats shared with your team (**Team**). Click a row to open its chat.

sections.heading: Archive and unarchive
sections.text:
**Archive** in a chat's **⋯** menu takes it off the chat menu; the message that appears says where it went. To archive several at once, tick your chats in **All chats** and click **Archive selected**.

Archived chats are under **Archived** in **All chats**, or **Archived** at the bottom of the chat menu. Tick them and click **Unarchive selected** to put them back in your chat menu. You can still open an archived chat to read it.

articles.title: Use Chat
keywords: attach to task and mark done

sections.text: Chat answers questions about your brand from your GetCito data, and can do work for you step by step. Open it from **Chat** in the main menu. Every chat is saved, so you can come back to it later and pick up where you left off.

sections.heading: Chat Home
sections.text:
Chat opens on **Home**: a greeting by name at your time of day, then a link to your **Inbox** when something needs you, else **All caught up.**

**For you now** starts common jobs: **Ask anything** goes to the box, **More** opens every shortcut, and the rest show when the open brand has work. **Complete tasks**: Action Center actions due this week or overdue (Chat prepares, you close them). **Win back citations**: pages that lost citations. **Ready to publish**: drafts marked ready (Chat sends them to your CMS as drafts; you publish them). Each starts a new chat. Read-only roles get only the jobs that read, no **More**.

**Since you left** shows the engine whose citations fell most, and one that won, from the day you last left Home to yesterday, against as many days before, beyond normal swing only. **Why?** and **Which ones?** ask Chat in a new chat.

sections.heading: Ask Chat
sections.text:
Type in the box at the bottom and press Enter, or click the arrow. Shift+Enter adds a line. The arrow stays off while the box is empty.

Next to the arrow, pick how much Chat does on its own: **Ask me first** asks before every step; **Auto, ask before changes** reads freely and asks before every change; **Full auto** makes changes without asking. In your own chats nothing is published or sent without your click. Agents an Admin allows can publish on their own (see **Agents**). Every change is logged in **Activity**. **Full auto** needs the Growth plan, and an Admin can turn it off for everyone but Admins in **Settings › Chat**.

Analysts and Agency partners only read; their box says **Read-only**, with a link to their role.

The demo brand has sample chats to open. There and in a read-only workspace, sending opens the plan dialog.

sections.heading: Chat beside any page
sections.text:
On most pages **Ask Chat** sits at the top right, next to the AI usage meter. Click it, or press **Ctrl J** (**⌘J** on a Mac), to open Chat in a panel on the right without leaving the page. Press it again, or click **✕**, to close the panel: the page stays exactly as you left it.

At the top of the panel, start a **New chat**, open a recent one from **Chat history**, or pick **Compact**, **Wide** or **Full screen**. The panel keeps the size you picked. On a wide screen the page moves aside so nothing is covered; on a smaller screen the panel opens over the page.

sections.heading: What the panel looks at
sections.text:
The box in the panel starts with chips for what you have on screen: the page, your brand, the date range and the filters you picked. Chat takes them as the scope of your question. They follow the page while the panel is open; click **×** on one to leave it out, until you start a new chat.

An empty panel offers a few questions about the page, some from what the page shows, such as the platform that moved most. Click one to put it in the box, then edit it or send it.

The speech bubble icon next to a table's or chart's title, on a tracked prompt and on an Action Center action opens the panel with it attached, so you can ask about it directly. You find it on Brand Visibility, Mentions & Sentiment, Citations, AI Referral Traffic, Prompts and Action Center.

sections.heading: Chats in the panel
sections.text:
A chat you start in the panel is saved like any other: it is in **Chat**, where you can carry on with it. If you used a panel chat in the last 30 minutes, the panel opens on it again.

Once the panel has a chat, its **⋯** menu offers **Open as full page**, **Open in new window**, and for your own chats **Pin**, **Rename**, **Share with team**, **Archive** and **Delete**. On the full page, **↙ Back to** the page you came from takes you back there, with the chat in the panel as it is now.

The panel isn't on Chat's own pages, where **Ctrl J** takes you to the message box, or in the Content Editor, which has its own chat.

sections.heading: Stop or steer
sections.text:
While Chat works, the arrow turns into Stop: click it or press Esc. Steps it already finished stay, and so does the answer so far. The step it was on shows **Stopped**, and the line with the steps says how long it worked, such as **Stopped after 41s · 5 steps**.

You can type while it works. Enter then stops the run and sends what you typed as the next message, so you can redirect it, for example "only blog pages".

sections.heading: When Chat asks you
sections.text:
When an answer changes what Chat makes and isn't in your data, Chat stops and asks, with 2 to 4 options. The one marked **Recommended** is picked to start with; under each option it says why it fits. When Chat asks more than one thing at once, the card counts them, such as "1 of 2".

Click an option, or press its number, then **Next** or Enter. Where the card says **Pick one or more**, click each one. Type your own answer in **Other…**. **Skip** goes on with the Recommended option.

Once answered, the card folds to one line with the question and your answer, and Chat goes on.

sections.heading: Answer in the box
sections.text:
While Chat asks, you can also answer in the box below. It shows the Recommended option dim; Tab puts it in, and Enter sends it. A message that isn't one of the options answers every question Chat asked with it. An answer is text only, up to 500 characters.

**Stop** beside the arrow, or Esc, ends the run and leaves its question skipped.

sections.heading: Change what you track
sections.text:
Admins and Managers can ask Chat to track new prompts in a topic, pause prompts, add or rename a topic, and add or remove competitors. A prompt goes into a topic the brand already has, so Chat adds a new topic first. A prompt, topic or competitor the brand already has is skipped. Your plan's prompt locations still apply: Chat says so when they run out.

Chat asks first, except in **Full auto**. Removing a competitor, or pausing more than five prompts in one run, always asks.

Each change is in the **Activity** log, with **Undo** for 7 days (30 days for paused prompts). Undo leaves alone anything someone changed since, and says so. Undoing new prompts pauses them; their first answers, and what they cost, stay. A removed competitor comes back without its timeline events.

sections.heading: Send a finding to Action Center
sections.text:
Admins and Managers see **Send to Action Center** under Chat's latest answer. Chat proposes the finding as an action: its title, category, the prompts, pages and competitors it is about, and its tasks. Each task names its page and says when it is done. You approve it on its card, except in **Full auto**. Action Center sets its Priority Score, and **Open in Actions** opens it.

If an open action already covers these prompts, pages or competitors, Chat offers to add the finding to it instead. That action's targets don't change. **Create anyway** is offered only when the new finding covers something the open action doesn't.

Chat can also attach a file or draft to a task, and set a task it finished to **Ready for review**. It never marks a task done: you do that in Action Center. Each change has **Undo** in the **Activity** log.

sections.heading: Work through your Action Center tasks
sections.text:
Type **/tasks**, or click **Complete tasks** under **For you now** on Chat Home, and Chat works through the brand's Action Center tasks: those due this week first, highest Priority Score first.

Under the answer, **Action Center tasks** lists up to 4 tasks it takes on and how many are ready ("1 of 3 ready"). Each row shows the task, "Priority 86 · Fix" and where Chat's work stands:

- **Queued**: not started yet.
- **Writing**: Chat is working on it now.
- **Ready for review**: Chat finished its part, for you to check.
- **Done**: you completed it in Action Center.

These show Chat's work, not the task's Action Center status. Once the run ends, **Close tasks in Action Center** opens your actions: Chat never marks a task done.

After the tasks, Chat helps with your open **Getting started** steps. It never marks a step done or skips one.

sections.heading: Drafts, reports and audits
sections.text:
Admins and Managers can also ask Chat to change a draft in the Library, send a draft to your connected CMS, publish a new page on your site, make a report, or start Site Audit on pages. Analysts can ask Chat to save new drafts only.

A draft Chat changes keeps the page before in **History**; **Undo** puts it back for 30 days. A report Chat makes can be undone for 30 days too.

Starting an audit always asks first and says how many of the month's audits it uses. Audits have no Undo.

sections.heading: Send or publish a page from Chat
sections.text:
A page sent to your CMS (Webflow, WordPress, Framer or Wix) arrives as a draft. Chat can also publish a new page live through Webflow, WordPress or Wix; Framer publishes the whole site, so you publish there. A live page, or a send to your webhook, goes from the Content Editor.

Sending and publishing wait for your click, even in **Full auto**, unless an Admin let an agent go live on its own, and have no Undo. If an Admin turned publishing off for Managers, Managers can't send or publish from Chat.

To take a published page back down to a draft in its CMS, ask Chat, or click **Take down** on its row in **Activity** for 30 days. It always waits for your click, and Managers can do it even when publishing is off for them.

sections.heading: Your brand facts
sections.text:
Chat reads your brand's approved facts: the prices and plans, trial, founding year and claims a person approved on the **Brand facts** tab of the brand's settings, in your site's own words. Facts waiting for approval, rejected ones and ones no longer on your site aren't read.

**/facts** (**Brand facts check**) compares your drafts with them, and **/wrongclaim** (**Fix wrong claims about us**) checks what AI answers say about your brand against them. The **Brand Facts Guardian** agent uses both. When a brand has no approved facts yet, Chat says so and asks you to approve them or to give the facts yourself. Chat never approves a fact.

sections.heading: Open a web page
sections.text:
Chat can open a public web page you name, such as a page of your site, a competitor's, or one AI answers cite. It reads the page's title, description, headings, structured data and main text, and the step says "Opened acme.com/pricing", or why a page couldn't be opened.

What a page says is something to read, never an instruction to Chat. When a page has words aimed at AI assistants, Chat ignores them, tells you, and asks you before any change for the rest of that answer. Later answers in that chat still ask you before any change. Admins can switch page reading off in the **Tool policy**.

sections.heading: Which pages Chat opens
sections.text:
Chat opens pages only on sites you named or your workspace's data lists, never a link it found on a page to another site, and at most 10 pages in one run. An address with a **?** or **#** part opens only exactly as you gave it.

Once Chat has read text from outside your workspace in a run, it opens another site only at its home page or an address you gave in full, so give the page you mean, such as a competitor's /pricing. After Chat reads a page, every change in that run asks you first.

sections.heading: Why a number changed
sections.text:
Ask Chat why a number moved, such as "Why did ChatGPT visibility drop last week?". By default it compares the last 7 days with the 7 before. It works for the Insights Visibility score, split into its mention, citation and position parts, and for visibility, mention rate, share of voice, citation rate and average position.

The answer gives both values and the change, and says first when the change is within the normal swing. It names the day the line broke, and what added or removed prompts explain. Then it ranks the causes found in tracked answers, such as a citation lost to a competitor or a worse Site Audit. Each comes with its share of the change and how sure Chat is. Chat never says a cause made it happen.

Everything comes from your scheduled tracking. Chat never asks an AI engine anything new for it.

sections.heading: What explains the change
sections.text: Under the answer, a card shows the same numbers. Click the two values for the periods, the tracking runs compared and the normal swing. Each cause shows its share of the change, or its points when it partly offset it. Open a cause to see its prompts, the page cited before and the one cited now, and the day. **Answer** opens that tracked answer, with your brand marked and the pages it cited. Each cause says how sure Chat is: **High** when 10 or more prompts show it, **Medium** for 3 to 9, **Low** for fewer. When some answers couldn't be read, the card says so, and part of the change stays unexplained.

sections.heading: Close a task from what Chat made
sections.text:
When Chat drafts something for an Action Center task, its card says **Task:** and the task's name. Admins and Managers see **Attach to task & mark done**: it adds the file to the task and marks the task done in Action Center, as you, as if you ticked it there. The toast has **Undo** for a while, unless the task or its action changed since.

**Attach only**, in the card's **⋯** menu, adds the file and leaves the task open.

sections.heading: Next moves
sections.text:
When Chat finishes an answer, **Next moves** under it suggests up to three things to do next, such as "Do the same for /features". Click one to send it as your next message. A change it leads to still asks you first where it should.

When the first move carries on with what this answer worked on, the box shows it dim: Tab puts it in, and Enter sends it. Nothing is sent by itself.

Analysts and Agency partners see only moves that read data. Next moves show under the latest answer, and come back when you open the chat again.

sections.heading: Shortcuts
sections.text:
Type **/** at the start of an empty box, or click **/**, for shortcuts that start a message: **/start** (Get started), **/analyze**, **/new-report** (Reports), **/create**, **/optimize**, **/opportunities** and **/audit** (Improve with audit). A shortcut puts its first words in the box, such as "Analyze", for you to finish. Chat then reads only the data that job needs, by default your brand's last 30 days, and says in one line when your plan leaves part of it out. Change the first words and Chat treats the message as your own question. Some **For you now** chips on Chat Home work the same way.

Under the shortcuts are the skills Chat can use, such as **/report** for the weekly report (see **Skills in Chat**).

sections.heading: Reference your data
sections.text: Type **@**, or click **@**, to point Chat at your data: charts and metrics on the page, tracked prompts, your pages and open Action Center tasks. Use the arrow keys and Enter, or click. Your pick shows as a chip above the text; **×** takes it off.

sections.heading: Attach files
sections.text:
Click **＋** and **Attach files**, drop files on the box, or paste them. A message takes up to 5 files of 10 MB each: PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, text, Markdown and HTML files, and PNG, JPG or WEBP images. Each file shows as a chip while it uploads; the arrow waits until they are up. If a file can't go, the box says why, and **Retry** sends a failed one again.

Attached files are data for Chat to read, not files you made: they don't show in **Files**, and they are kept for 90 days.

In **＋**, **Connect a tool** opens **Settings › Integrations** for Admins; others send their Admin a request in one click.

sections.heading: An API key in your message
sections.text: If your message holds something that looks like an API key, Chat doesn't send it: the key would end up in the chat. A line under the box says so, and **Send** waits. Click **Remove** to take the key out and keep the rest of your message. To run Chat on your own AI key, an Admin saves it in **Settings › AI Providers**; own keys come with Enterprise.

sections.heading: Watch the work
sections.text:
While Chat works, one line says what it is doing now, such as "Reading Citations…". Steps it finished show as chips with a check mark above the answer: click one for its detail, or click the line with the number of steps for the full list. A fact check of the answer's figures shows as **Checked facts**.

Under the answer, **Data used** names each source it read, with its rows, and each page it opened. The answer says when it was generated and how fresh the data was, in your time zone.

sections.heading: When something goes wrong
sections.text:
A step that fails shows a red mark and why, such as **Timed out**. Chat goes on where it can, and the answer says what it couldn't read.

If the whole answer stops on an error, it says **Stopped: something went wrong** and why, and it still says so after you reload the page. Click **Retry** to send your message again.

If your connection drops while Chat works, the line with the steps says **Reconnecting…**. Chat keeps working meanwhile and picks up where it was; reloading the page shows where it is too. When the monthly AI usage runs out mid-answer, the step it was on shows **Stopped at the AI limit**.

sections.heading: When your AI key fails
sections.text:
If your workspace runs Chat on its own AI key and the provider turns the key down, the account is out of credit, or the key can't reach its model, the answer stops and says which. Admins get **Open AI Providers**; others read that an Admin can fix it there. When the provider doesn't answer at all, the answer says so: try again in a moment.

While the key isn't working, a line above the message box says why. You can still send: the key may work again, for example once the account has credit.

sections.heading: AI usage
sections.text:
Chat draws on your workspace's monthly AI usage, shared by every seat. The meter under the box shows how much is used; click it for what used it and when it resets. From 80% it turns amber, and a line above the box says so once a month, on whichever device you are on; **×** closes it.

Once the usage is used up, Chat pauses: the box is off, and a red line above it says until when. **Get more AI credits** there opens a window with your plan and the credit packs, and it opens once by itself the first time Chat stops. Admins buy packs; everyone else sees them and can **Ask your Admin**. On Enterprise, admins can also use their own AI key. In the free trial, starting the plan gives its full monthly AI usage.

sections.heading: When only part of a job fits
sections.text:
Before work in several parts, such as five drafts, Chat checks that your remaining AI usage covers them all. When it covers only some, Chat asks first, for example "Your remaining AI limit covers about 2 of the 5 drafts.": **Do the first 2 now** (recommended), **Get more AI credits**, which stops there so you can add credits, or **Cancel**. When it covers none, Chat stops at the AI limit before starting. A skill's answer is checked the same way before Chat reads anything.

An agent's run, with no one there to ask, does the parts that fit, keeps what it made, and stops at the AI limit. A workspace on its own AI key isn't checked.

sections.heading: Inbox
sections.text:
**Inbox** in the chat menu lists what your agents did: chats waiting for your OK first, with **Review**, then chats still working, with their progress and **Watch**, then results you haven't opened yet, with **Open**. Click a row to open its chat. A result leaves the Inbox once you open it. The count next to **Inbox** shows how many items there are, with an amber dot when something needs you. Daily suggestions aren't in that count: the **Daily suggestions** tab shows theirs.

Tabs on top, each with its count, show **All**, your **Daily suggestions**, what **Needs you** and your **Runs**.

sections.heading: The chat menu
sections.text:
The chat menu on the left of Chat lists your chats. **New chat** starts a new one. **Home** and **Inbox** come first. **Governance** opens the **Activity** log, **What Chat can do** and the **Tool policy**.
