**Agents at work** lists the chats that need your OK, the ones still working, and finished results you haven't opened yet, with the step each one is on. It shows three at a time: **See all** lists the rest. A dot shows each chat's state; click **?** to see what the dots mean.

**Chats** lists every other chat, newest first, under **Pinned**, **Today**, **Yesterday**, **Previous 7 days**, **Previous 30 days**, then by month. A chat a teammate shared shows their initials. **Search chats** above them finds a chat by its words, and **All chats** and **Archived** at the end list every chat.

sections.heading: Hide the chat menu
sections.text: Click the panel button next to **New chat**, or press Ctrl+\ (⌘\ on a Mac), to hide the menu and give the chat the whole width. A small bar at the top then keeps **New chat** and your runs at hand. Chat remembers your choice on every device. On a narrow window the menu opens over the page instead. Ctrl+Shift+O (⌘⇧O) starts a new chat from anywhere in Chat.

sections.heading: Move around Chat
sections.text:
Pages under Chat, such as **Inbox** and **All chats**, show **← Back to Chat** at the top left, next to where you are, such as Chat › All chats. It takes you back to the chat you last had open in this tab, or to Chat Home. Click **Chat** in the path for Chat Home; **Chat** in the main menu always opens Chat Home too.

Esc closes only the box or menu on top, such as search or a **⋯** menu, and never leaves the page.

In Chat, the main menu on the left is a narrow bar of icons, so the chat has room. Point at it to see it whole, or click the GetCito logo to keep it open; click the logo again to make it narrow. Chat remembers your choice on every device.

sections.heading: Manage a chat
sections.text:
Point at a chat in the menu and click **⋯**, or click **⋯** at the top right of an open chat:

- **Pin** keeps it under **Pinned** at the top of the menu; **Unpin** puts it back under its day.
- **Rename** lets you type a new name in place. Press Enter to save or Esc to cancel. You can also double-click a chat's name in the menu.
- **Archive** takes it off the menu. It waits under **All chats › Archived**, where **Unarchive selected** brings it back.
- **Delete** asks first, then deletes the chat for everyone. Click **Undo** within a few seconds to bring it back. A chat that is still working is stopped first.
- **Open in new window** opens it in another browser window.

**Export chat** downloads the whole chat as **Markdown**, **Word** or **PDF**: each question under "You" and its answer after it.

sections.heading: Copy, download or save an answer
sections.text:
Under every finished answer, three small buttons show their names when you point at them:

- **Copy** copies the answer, with its formatting where you paste it.
- **Download** gives the answer as **Markdown**, **Word** or **PDF**, and as **CSV** or **Excel** when it has a table (one sheet per table). The file is named after your question and the day, and it carries when the answer was made and how fresh its data was. Downloads aren't kept and use no AI.
- **Save to Files** keeps the answer for your whole workspace; it then reads **In Files**. Saved answers count toward your workspace's storage: 1 GB in the free trial, 5 GB on Starter, 25 GB on Growth, and what your contract says on Enterprise. When storage is full, the answer isn't saved, and the button says so.

Every role can copy, download and save answers it can open.

sections.heading: What Chat makes
sections.text:
When Chat makes something for you, such as a page saved as a Content draft, it shows under the answer as a card with its name and type. It is also kept in **Files** for your whole workspace, and the card says **In Files**. From the card, **Copy** copies it, **Download** gives it in the formats it has (for a page: HTML, Markdown, Word or PDF), and **Open in Content Editor** opens the page to keep working on it. When storage is full, the card says it wasn't saved to Files, with **Get more storage** to add a storage pack. Click **Files** in the chat menu to find, copy or download everything kept there.

The pen button under an answer, **Open in Content Editor**, turns the answer itself into a new Content draft in your brand and opens it.

sections.heading: Share a chat with your team
sections.text: A chat is yours alone until you share it. **Share with team** lets everyone in your workspace open it and read it; they can't change it, and their box says so, with **Start your own chat**. **Stop sharing** makes it private again. A shared chat shows its author's initials in teammates' menus, and an Admin can delete it.

sections.heading: Old Agent links
sections.text:
Chat replaces the earlier Agent page. Links and bookmarks to the Agent page open Chat instead, and a link to one of your chats opens that chat.

The first time you open Chat, your chats from the Agent page are copied in, so they are in the chat menu with your other chats, by the date of their last message. Your questions and the answers are kept; the steps the Agent took to find them are not. A chat the Agent page never named is called **New chat**.

sections.heading: A chat that isn't available
sections.text: If a chat was deleted, or it belongs to someone else and isn't shared with you, Chat says **This chat isn't available.** Click **New chat** to start a new one.

articles.title: Change your Chat settings

sections.text: **Settings** in the chat menu holds your own Chat preferences. They are yours alone and follow you to every device. A change is kept as soon as you make it; if it can't be kept, it goes back and Chat says so. The bar next to **Settings** shows how much of this month's AI usage your workspace has used.

sections.heading: Default mode
sections.text: **Default mode** is how much the agent does on its own when you start a job: **Ask me first**, **Auto, ask before changes** or **Full auto**. New chats start in it. In your own chats nothing is published or sent without your click. Agents an Admin allows can publish on their own. **Full auto** needs the Growth plan, and your Admin can turn it off for everyone but Admins; when it is locked, point at it to see why. Analysts and Agency partners only read, so they have no default mode.

sections.heading: Your focus
sections.text: **Your focus** lists the eight areas Chat can focus on for you, such as **Competitors** or **Content**. Tick the ones you work on: Chat Home and its suggestions follow them. Your focus doesn't change what you can do; your role decides that.

sections.heading: Answer language
sections.text: **Answer language** sets the language Chat answers in. **Same as my question**, the default, answers in the language you write in. Pick a language, such as English, and Chat answers in it whatever language you write in: useful for agencies and teams that write in several languages. Asking for a language in a message, such as "answer in German", always wins for that answer. The app itself stays in English.

sections.heading: Chat on every page
sections.text:
**Open Chat on every page** shows or hides **Ask Chat** with Ctrl J in each page's header.

Workspace rules, such as which tools Chat may use on its own, are in **Tool policy**; only Admins change them.

articles.title: Get daily suggestions in your Chat Inbox

sections.text: Each morning Chat can pick one action that waits in your Action Center and put it in your **Inbox**, with what it would take, so your open actions get done. It picks from what is already there, by its priority, and adds no new work. Picking costs no AI usage.

sections.heading: The Inbox tabs
sections.text:
The **Inbox** has tabs on top, each with its count:

- **All**: everything below.
- **Daily suggestions**: the actions picked for you.
- **Needs you**: chats waiting for your OK.
- **Runs**: chats still working, and results you haven't opened.

The line under **Inbox** counts what needs you, what runs and the suggestions of this week.

sections.heading: Daily suggestions
sections.text:
You get at most one a day for each brand, and at most 7 a week. Each row shows the action's title, its number in the Action Center, its priority, how it can be done, such as **Content Editor or Chat · about 20 min**, and the day it came. With more than one brand, each row also names its brand.

The dot shows where it stands: blue while it's new, no longer blue once you've seen it, and green once you started it. The list shows the last 7 days only.

When the action is done or dismissed in the Action Center, its row stays, faded, with **Done** or **Dismissed**. When the action is deleted, its suggestion leaves the list.

Click a row, or **Open**, to open the suggestion's page, on its brand.

sections.heading: The suggestion's page
sections.text:
The page asks the action's title as a question and answers it: **Picked for you today · no AI cost**, what Chat read, then why this action, why now and how long it takes.

The **From your Action Center** card shows the action, its tasks and its pages. **Open** opens it in the Action Center. Two buttons start the work:

- **Content Editor**: opens the action's draft, when it has writing to do.
- **Do it with Chat**: starts a chat about the action, in your Chat mode.

You can also tell Chat what to do in the box at the bottom. That starts the same chat, which counts toward your AI usage like any chat.

**Not now** brings it back in a week if the action is still open. **Remove this suggestion** takes it off your **Inbox**: the action stays in the Action Center.

sections.heading: Who gets them
sections.text: Daily suggestions come from the Action Center, which is in everyone's menu, so menu settings don't turn them off. Admins and Managers get them for every brand they can see. Agency partners get them once they open the **Inbox** for the first time. Analysts don't get them. The demo brand gets none, and a workspace whose plan ended gets no new ones: its list keeps what it has.

sections.heading: Pause or turn them back on
sections.text:
Click **Pause daily suggestions**, on the **Daily suggestions** tab, to stop them for all your brands. Your Action Center is unchanged.

When you haven't opened, started, put off or removed any brand's suggestion for 30 days, Chat stops picking them for that brand and says **Daily suggestions are paused**. Seeing them in the **Inbox** doesn't count as using them.

Click **Turn back on** to start them again for all your brands: the first one arrives the next morning.

articles.title: Find and download what Chat made in Files

sections.text: **Files** keeps everything Chat finished for your workspace: pages it saved and answers you saved to Files. Everyone in your workspace can see and download them. Files are kept for 1 year.

sections.heading: Open Files
sections.text:
Click **Files** in the chat menu, under **Settings**. You can also press Ctrl K (⌘K on a Mac) in Chat and type "Files". The newest files come first, 50 at a time; click **Show more** at the bottom to see older ones.

Each row shows:

- The file's name and the formats it comes in, and **Used in Content draft** when it was opened in the Content Editor.
- **Made by**: you, a teammate, **Agent** (an Action Center task) or **Scheduled** (a scheduled job).
- **From chat**: the chat it was made in. Click it to open that chat. It shows only for chats you can open.
- **Updated**: when it was made, and **Data as of** when it used your workspace data. Hover over it to see the time zone.

sections.heading: Find a file
sections.text: Use the filters above the list: **All** (with how many files your workspace has), **Drafts**, **Reports**, **Code**, **Tables**, **Images**, **From me** and **From agents**. Type in **Filter by name…** to see the files whose name has every word you typed. A few letters are enough. When nothing matches, click **Clear filters**.

sections.heading: Copy, open and download
sections.text:
- **Copy** copies the file's text as Markdown.
- **Open** opens a page in the Content Editor, when it was saved as a Content draft.
- **Download** gives the file in one of its formats: for a page HTML, Markdown, Word or PDF; for a saved answer Markdown, Word or PDF, plus CSV and Excel when it has a table.

To download several files at once, tick them and click **Download selected**. You get one .zip file with each file in its main format. You can download up to 50 files and 100 MB at a time.

sections.heading: Storage
sections.text:
The meter at the top right shows how much storage your workspace uses, for example "Storage 2.1 of 25 GB". Your plan includes 1 GB in the free trial, 5 GB on Starter, 25 GB on Growth, and what your contract says on Enterprise. The meter turns amber at 80%.

When storage is full, a line under the title says so. Chat still shows new work in its chat as a card, but it isn't saved to Files, so the card can't copy or download it; the answer above it can still be copied and downloaded. Files you already have are never deleted because storage is full. Click **Get more storage** on that line, on the card, or on the meter to add a storage pack.

articles.title: Choose what Chat focuses on

sections.text: You can tell Chat what to focus on for you: one or more areas, such as **Competitors**, **Content** or **Product and buyer needs**. Focus changes only what Chat suggests. What you can do still comes from your role.

sections.heading: Pick your focus
sections.text:
The first time you open Chat, it asks **What should Chat focus on for you?** Pick one or more of the eight areas and select **Continue**. The areas that match what you work on, from your menu settings, start out picked.

**Skip for now** keeps the default Home. Chat asks only once, whichever you choose.

sections.heading: What changes on Chat Home
sections.text:
With a focus, the chips under **For you now** come from your areas, taken in turn so each one shows: for example **Competitor moves**, **Fact check** or **Buyer questions**. **Complete tasks**, **Win back citations** and **Ready to publish** keep their counts and show only when there is something to do.

**Start with a question** offers four questions from your areas, filled with your own competitors, topics and markets where GetCito knows them. Select one to start a new chat with it.

**New for you** lists up to four new skills for your areas, such as **Rival brief** or **Buyer questions**; select one to start a chat with it.

With **Competitors** picked, the line under the greeting can say when a competitor's mention rate rose this week. The skills in the **/** menu list your areas' skills first.

sections.heading: Change it later
sections.text:
Under the greeting on Chat Home, a line shows your focus, such as **Focused on Product and Markets and sources**. Select **Edit** to open the picker with your picks on; **Cancel** leaves your focus as it was. With no focus, the line says **Get suggestions for what you work on**; select **Choose focus**.

You can also change it in **Settings** in the chat menu, under **Your focus**. Each change is kept at once and follows you to every device. Clear every box to go back to the default Home.

sections.heading: What focus doesn't change
sections.text: Focus never gives you more or less access. What you can change still depends on your role, whatever you pick, and an Admin's menu settings stay as they are.

articles.title: Skills in Chat

sections.text: Skills teach Chat how to do a task the way GetCito recommends: what to read, the steps to take and what the result looks like. Chat has twenty-one GetCito skills, such as **Win back lost citations**, **FAQ from fan-outs**, **Ready to publish**, **Weekly report**, **Buyer questions** and **Rival brief**.

sections.heading: Use a skill
sections.text:
Type **/** at the start of an empty box, or click **/**. Under the shortcuts, **Skills** lists each skill by its command and name. Type to filter, such as **/fa** for **/faq**, then press Enter or click. The command goes first in the box: finish your message after it and send.

You can also type a skill's command yourself, at the start of your message. One answer uses up to three skills, a shortcut's own steps counted. **/report** is the **Weekly report** skill; for any other report, use the **/new-report** shortcut (**Reports**).

sections.heading: The Skills page
sections.text:
Open **Skills** in the Chat menu to see every skill. **GetCito skills** lists GetCito's, and **All**, **Content**, **Brand Visibility**, **Product Visibility**, **Technical** and **Reports** narrow them. **My skills** lists your workspace's own, with where each came from and whether it waits for review.

A card shows the connections the skill uses on the brand you have open: green when connected, grey when not. **Run** starts a chat with the skill. **Schedule** opens Chat with "Every Monday at 9:00, /skill" in the box, to change before you send. **Create agent** starts an agent on it.

Admins turn a skill on or off for the whole workspace, and you turn your own saved skills on or off. Click a skill's name to see its details, share it with your workspace or delete it.

sections.heading: When Chat picks a skill
sections.text:
Chat also picks a skill by itself when one fits your question. Either way, the steps above the answer show **Used skill:** with the skill's name, and where it comes from under it: **GetCito library**, or **You** for a skill you saved. A shortcut shows **Used shortcut:** with its name.

Analysts and Agency partners have no **/** menu, but Chat still uses a skill for them when one fits.

sections.heading: Save your own skill
sections.text: Admins and Managers can ask Chat to keep steps they repeat as a skill of their own, for example: "Save this as a skill called /pricing-brief: open with the answer, then three short sections." Chat shows the skill's name, what it does and its steps on a card, and saves it when you approve, or by itself in Full auto. The skill is private to you and joins your **/** menu right away. It can't take the name of a GetCito skill or a shortcut, such as **/analyze**, and your plan sets how many skills your workspace keeps.

sections.heading: Import a skill
sections.text:
Admins and Managers on a paid plan can bring in a skill from outside. On the **Skills** page, click **New skill**, then **Upload a SKILL.md or .zip** (up to 5 MB), or **Import from GitHub** and paste a public github.com link. Only the skill's instructions come in: scripts, commands and allowed tools are removed, and nothing runs. A GitHub skill is read at today's commit and never updates by itself. Only MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD and ISC licenses are accepted.

An imported skill stays off until an Admin reviews it. **Review** shows the cleaned file with any hidden characters marked, what the safety scan found, what was removed and where it came from. The Admin approves or rejects it; a skill the scan blocks can't be approved. A Manager's import asks the Admins to review it.

sections.heading: Updates to an imported skill
sections.text: Once a week, GetCito checks the source of each approved GitHub skill. When its SKILL.md changed, its card in **My skills** shows **Update available**. **Review update** shows what changed, line by line, and the safety scan of the new version. Nothing changes until an Admin clicks **Approve update**, and the new version is cleaned and scanned again first. A skill whose saved file was changed some other way is turned off.

sections.heading: What a skill can't change
sections.text: A skill shapes how Chat works, not what it may do. It gives Chat no new tools, doesn't skip the card a change waits on, and doesn't publish by itself: only an agent an Admin allows may send pages on its own. Your role, your plan and your workspace's Chat settings still decide what Chat can change, and a change still asks you first where it should.

sections.heading: The GetCito skills
sections.text: Win back lost citations, Complete this week’s tasks, Quality pass, FAQ from fan-outs, Weekly report, Beat a competitor, Refresh for this year, Ready to publish, AI shopping readiness, Fix wrong claims about us, Answer-first rewrite, Brand facts check, Comparison page and Translate a page.

articles.title: Citations page

sections.text: The **Citations** page lists the domains and URLs that AI engines cited in their answers to your tracked prompts, for the brand selected in the sidebar. It shows which sources AI engines rely on when they answer questions in your category, and sorts them by source type. It reads the answers your tracking already collects.

sections.heading: Filters
sections.text:
- **Date Range**: 24h (the default), 7d, 30d, 90d, All or Custom.
- **Topic**: one topic. It's shown only when the brand has topics.
- **Prompt**: one tracked prompt; type to search the list.
- **Platform**: one AI platform, or all of them.
- **Region**: one region the answers were tracked in, or all of them.

The filters are kept in the page's address, so a refresh or a shared link opens the same view. When a table is empty for the window but the brand has citations outside it, **Show all data** clears the filters and shows all dates and all sources.

sections.heading: Summary cards
sections.text:
Three cards sit at the top of the page:

- **Total Citations**: every citation in the window, across the tracked results (AI answers) in it.
- **Unique Domains**: the cited domains in the source choice you made (**Brand**, **Competitors**, **Third-Party** or **All**), with their unique URLs.
- **Avg citations per result**: the number of links per AI answer.

sections.heading: Top Sources and the source choice
sections.text:
The **Top Sources** card has four tabs: **Domains**, **URLs**, **Competitor Gaps** and **Source Types**.

Above the Domains and URLs tables, four buttons choose which sources they list:

- **Brand** (the default): your brand's own domains.
- **Competitors**: the domains of the competitors you track.
- **Third-Party**: every other site.
- **All**: every source.

The choice doesn't change **Total Citations**, **Avg citations per result**, **Competitor Gaps** or **Source Types**.

sections.heading: The Domains tab
sections.text:
The **Domains** tab ranks each cited domain by how often it was cited, with these columns:

- **Domain**: the domain, its source type, and a link that opens the site.
- **Platforms**: the AI platforms whose answers cited it.
- **Usage**: the share of tracked answers in the window that cite it.
- **Avg Citations**: how many times an answer that cites the domain cites it, on average.

On a domain that isn't yours or a tracked competitor's, the **+** button (**Add as competitor**) opens a dialog with a name taken from the domain. Edit the name and click **Add** to track it on the **Competitors** page.

sections.heading: The URLs tab
sections.text:
The **URLs** tab ranks each cited page by its citations, with **Platforms**, **Usage** and **Citations**. Click a page's title to open its own page in GetCito, with every answer that cited it; the small icon beside the title opens the page itself.

The tab lists up to the 2,000 most-cited URLs, and its count gives the full number. Both the Domains and URLs tables show 100 rows a page.

sections.heading: Export CSV
sections.text:
**Export CSV** in the page header downloads the open tab, with the filters applied:

- **Domains**: each domain with its source type, citations, the answers citing it, its usage and the AI platforms.
- **URLs**: each page with its domain, source type, title, citations, the answers citing it and its usage.
- **Competitor Gaps**: the gap list, with each domain's source type, competitor answers, competitors and strength.

**Source Types** has no export.

sections.heading: Source types
sections.text:
GetCito gives every cited domain one of eight types:

- **You**: your brand's domains and their subdomains.
- **Competitor**: the domains of the competitors you track, and their subdomains.
- **Editorial**: a fixed list of well-known news, tech and magazine sites.
- **Forum**: forums and question-and-answer sites.
- **Social**: social networks, video sites and blogging platforms.
- **Review**: review and rating sites.
- **Institutional**: .edu, .gov and .mil addresses (country versions included), academic addresses such as .ac.uk, Wikipedia, and a list of public and international bodies.
- **Other**: every site that isn't on one of the lists.

You and Competitor come first: a tracked competitor's domain is always Competitor, even when it's also a review site. Only competitors with a domain are matched. The other lists are short, so most sites are Other.

sections.heading: The Source Types tab
sections.text: The **Source Types** tab shows the cited domains in a donut chart, with each type's share of the domains, not of the citations. It covers every cited domain in the window, whatever the source choice above the tables.

sections.heading: How to use the page
sections.text:
- **See which of your pages AI cites**: keep **Brand**, the default, and open the **URLs** tab. It lists your own pages that AI cites, on which platforms and how often. Open a page to see the prompts it's cited for.
- **Find the third-party sources AI trusts**: choose **Third-Party**. The top of the Domains and URLs lists are the sites AI leans on most for your prompts: places to be mentioned or cited.
- **Watch your competitors' pages**: choose **Competitors** to see which competitor domains and pages AI cites in your answers.
- **Find outreach targets**: the **Competitor Gaps** tab lists the third-party sites AI cites when it names a competitor and not you.

articles.title: Details of a cited URL

sections.text: Every URL that AI engines cite has its own page in GetCito. Open it from the **URLs** tab of the **Citations** page by clicking a page's title. It opens with the Citations page's date range, platform and region, but not its topic or prompt. You can change the date range and platform on the URL's page. **Citations** at the top goes back.

sections.heading: The header
sections.text:
The header shows the page's title and address, and its source type. When GetCito can tell from the address and title, it also shows the article type: **Topic Guide**, **How-to Guide**, **Review**, **Ranked List** or **Comparison**.

Your own pages are marked **Owned**. Any other page has **Add as competitor**, which adds the page's domain to your tracked competitors.

sections.heading: The summary cards
sections.text:
Five cards sum the page up:

- **Total citations**: how many times AI answers cited it in the window.
- **Answers citing**: how many answers cited it.
- **Prompts**: how many prompts those answers came from.
- **Platforms**: how many AI platforms cited it, and which.
- **Last seen**: when it was last cited, with the date it was first seen.

sections.heading: Extra cards for your own pages
sections.text:
On a page of your own, two more cards appear:

- **Targeted in N prompts**: the prompts that list this page in their **Target URLs**, and how many times it was cited for each.
- **AI-referred visits**: visits to this page from AI platforms in the window, by platform.

sections.heading: Cited in
sections.text:
**Cited in** lists every AI answer in the window that cites the page, newest first, 10 a page:

- **Date**: when the answer was tracked.
- **Platform**: the AI platform that gave the answer.
- **Prompt**: the prompt; click it to open the prompt's page.
- **Sentiment**: the answer's sentiment.
- **Brand mentioned**: a check when the AI answer names your brand. It says nothing about the cited page's own text.
- **Position**: where the page's first citation sits among the answer's citations: **Early**, **Mid** or **Late**, with its number, such as #2 of 7.

sections.heading: Prompts breakdown
sections.text: **Prompts breakdown** lists the prompts whose answers cite the page, with **Answers**, **Citations** and **Last seen**, the most citations first. Use it to see exactly which questions lead AI engines to this page.

sections.heading: Use what you find
sections.text:
- On one of your own pages, **Cited in** and **Prompts breakdown** show the prompts AI engines cite it for, on which platforms and how often.
- A third-party page that AI engines lean on for your prompts is a place to be mentioned or cited.
- A competitor's page shows which of your prompts send AI engines to that competitor. **Add as competitor** starts tracking a site that isn't on your list yet.

articles.title: Find where competitors are cited and you aren't

sections.text: **Competitor Gaps** is a tab of the **Top Sources** card on the **Citations** page. It lists the third-party domains that AI engines cite when they name a competitor and not you. These are outreach targets: sites AI engines already trust for your prompts, where a mention or a citation of your own is missing.

sections.heading: Gap list
By competitor
How Strength works
sections.text:
**Strength** weighs each answer by how many sources it had, so a source in a two-source answer counts more than one in a twenty-source answer. Hover **How this works** beside the views for a short note on the method.

When your brand appears in fewer than one answer in ten in the window, a note says the list may be broad. Work on your baseline visibility first.

sections.heading: Filters and export
sections.text:
Competitor Gaps follows the page's date, topic, prompt, platform and region filters. It doesn't follow the **Brand**, **Competitors**, **Third-Party** or **All** choice above the Domains and URLs tables.

**Export CSV** in the page header, with this tab open, downloads the gap list: each domain with its source type, competitor answers, competitors and strength.

sections.heading: Close a gap with these sources
sections.text:
1. On the **Competitors** page, find the prompts where a competitor leads you, under **Gaps**.
2. Here, in **By competitor**, see the sources AI cites with that competitor and not with you.
3. Create content for the prompt in **Content**.
4. Publish it, earn placements on those sources, and watch the prompt in the head-to-head comparison as new answers are tracked.

articles.title: Add competitors to track

sections.text: Competitors are the brands GetCito compares with yours in AI answers to your tracked prompts. You add and remove them on the **Competitors** page, right under **Reports** in the sidebar, and each one then appears in **Tracked Competitors** for a head-to-head comparison.

sections.heading: Open the Competitors page
Add a competitor
sections.text:
Click **Add Competitor** and fill in:

- **Name**: as AI answers write it, not the web address. GetCito looks for the name in every answer.
- **Domain** (optional): GetCito also looks for the domain in answers, counts citations of the competitor's pages, and marks those pages **Competitor** on the **Citations** page. The card that follows the competitor's pages over time needs it too.

Click **Add**.

sections.heading: Suggest competitors
sections.text:
**Suggest competitors** researches your brand on the web, from its website, region and language, and lists competitors with their domains. The ones you already track are left out.

All suggestions come ticked: untick the ones you don't want and click **Add N competitors**. **Refresh suggestions** asks again. The brand needs a website first.

sections.heading: Add a competitor from Citations
sections.text: On the **Citations** page, the **+** button (**Add as competitor**) on a cited domain that isn't yours or a tracked competitor's opens a dialog with a name taken from the domain. Edit the name and click **Add**. A cited URL's own page has **Add as competitor** too, which adds its domain.

sections.heading: When a new competitor is counted
sections.text:
A competitor is counted in the answers tracked after you add it; earlier answers aren't counted again. Until an answer in the date range is measured for it, its card says **No data**.

When a competitor is added, GetCito also reads back 90 days of your answers once, to find the first time AI cited one of its pages.

sections.heading: How many to track
sections.text:
The Getting started step asks for at least 3 competitors, and 5 to 20 give the clearest picture.

AI answers to your prompts may name brands you've never heard of. They are the alternatives people see when you're not cited. Add the most-mentioned ones to your competitors to track them properly.

sections.heading: Remove a competitor
sections.text: Hover the competitor's card in **Tracked Competitors**, click the bin icon, then **Yes, remove competitor**. It's no longer tracked. Past results keep their numbers, but they can't be linked back to the competitor.

sections.heading: When the workspace is read-only
sections.text: In cloud mode, while the workspace is read-only, **Add Competitor**, **Suggest competitors** and removing a competitor open the plan dialog instead.

articles.title: Compare your AI visibility with competitors

sections.text: The **Competitors** page, right under **Reports** in the sidebar, compares the AI visibility of the competitors you track with yours, across your tracked prompts and AI platforms. You can also open it with **Head-to-Head** on the **Leaderboard** card of **Brand Visibility**, or by clicking a competitor's name there. **Tracked Competitors** lists them with their visibility; select one to see it head-to-head with your brand.

sections.heading: Tracked Competitors
sections.text:
The **Tracked Competitors** card lists every competitor with its domain and:

- its AI Visibility Score from 0 to 100, the same score as on the Brand Visibility leaderboard: how often answers name it, cite its site, and how early it's named. Hover the score to see its answers, citations and position factor.
- the prompts it's visible in, out of the prompts with answers in the window, such as 12/40 prompts.

**No data** means no answer in the window was measured for that competitor yet, for example one you've just added.

The **Date Range** at the top (7d, 30d by default, 90d, All or Custom) sets the window for these scores. **Export CSV** on the card downloads your brand's and every competitor's scores, with their visible prompts, mentions and citations.

sections.heading: Open a head-to-head comparison
sections.text:
Click a competitor's card to compare it with your brand under **Your brand vs competitor**, with both names filled in. Click the card again to close the comparison. The selected competitor is kept in the page's address, so a refresh or a shared link opens the same one.

The comparison reads every tracked answer, not just the date range. Its scores are each answer's own visibility score from 0 to 100, for your brand and for the competitor.

When there's nothing to compare yet, it says **No comparison data**: run tracking for your prompts first.

sections.heading: Scores and Platform Breakdown
sections.text:
At the top of the comparison, **Your Avg. Score**, **Their Avg. Score** and **Score Difference** show your average score, the competitor's, and the difference between them.

**Platform Breakdown** shows your average and the competitor's on each AI platform, with the difference. A competitor can lead on one platform and trail on another, so aim your work at the platforms where it's ahead.

sections.heading: Gaps and Strengths
sections.text:
- **Gaps** lists up to 10 prompt and platform combinations where the competitor scores higher, grouped by prompt, the widest gap first.
- **Strengths** lists up to 10 where you score higher, your biggest lead first.

A prompt with several platforms opens to show each one.

sections.heading: Prompt-by-Prompt Comparison
sections.text:
**Prompt-by-Prompt Comparison** lists every prompt with **You**, **Them** and **Diff**, the most recently run first.

Click a prompt to see each platform, with its model and region, and how many runs it has. Click a platform with more than one run to see its **Previous runs**, with the date, both scores, the difference and the sentiment. The eye icon opens an AI answer.

**Export CSV** beside the comparison's title downloads it per prompt and platform: the model, region, runs, both scores, the difference and the latest run.

sections.heading: The competitor's pages over time
sections.text:
Below the comparison, a card shows why the competitor may be rising. Its chart shows the answers that mentioned the competitor, and your brand, each week for the last twelve weeks. A marker sits on each week something happened to its pages; the events are listed newest first:

- **First cited in your tracked answers**: the first day an AI answer to one of your prompts cited one of its pages. When a competitor is added, GetCito reads back 90 days of your answers once, so the first date is the first within that window.
- **Changed**: once a week, GetCito reads again the 10 competitor pages your answers cited most over the last two weeks. When a page's words changed by more than a date or a price moving, it says so, with the Site Audit checks it gained or lost, such as an FAQ or a table.

sections.heading: How the pages are read
sections.text:
The card needs the competitor's domain to find its pages. Pages are read for free from their public address, within a few reads a day, never from a site whose robots.txt keeps crawlers out. The brand's daily page reads are shared with the Action Center's tasks, which go first.

Only what Site Audit's checks found and a summary of the page's words are kept, never its text. Nothing is compared with another brand's answers.

sections.heading: Close a visibility gap
sections.text:
1. On **Gaps**, find the prompts where the competitor leads most.
2. Open the AI answer with the eye icon: what is the competitor named or cited for? The pages-over-time card shows whether its pages changed, and **Competitor Gaps** on the **Citations** page lists the sources AI cites with the competitor and not with you.
3. Create content for that prompt in **Content**.
4. Publish it, earn placements on those sources, and watch the prompt in the comparison as new answers are tracked.

articles.title: Connect Webflow, WordPress, Framer or Wix

sections.text: To send Content Editor pages straight to your CMS, connect it in **Settings › Integrations** with the brand selected. Each brand connects its own Webflow site, WordPress site, Framer project or Wix site. Only admins and managers can connect, change or disconnect a CMS; members see where the brand's pages go.

sections.heading: Connect Webflow
sections.text:
In the **Webflow** card, open **How to get a site token** and follow its steps to generate a site token in Webflow. Webflow shows the token only once. Paste it in **Site token** and click **Connect**.

Then pick the **Collection** your pages go to, your blog's for example. If the token reaches more than one site, pick the **Site** first. Under **Which field takes what**, choose the field for the page content and, if you like, the meta title, meta description, structured data and date. The page's title and slug always go to the item's Name and Slug. Click **Save**. If the collection requires a field GetCito doesn't fill, **Save** names it: make it optional in Webflow first.

sections.heading: Connect WordPress
sections.text:
In WordPress, sign in as the user pages should be written by. A separate user with the **Author** role is enough, since GetCito writes drafts only. Under **Users › Profile**, add an **Application Password** named GetCito and copy it; WordPress shows it once.

In the **WordPress** card, enter the **Site address** as you visit the site, the **User** and the **Application Password**, and click **Connect**. Paste the Application Password, not the user's own password. The site must use https. GetCito checks the site before it keeps anything.

sections.heading: If WordPress won't connect
sections.text:
A message says why. The most common fixes:

- WordPress refused the user or password: check the user name, and paste the Application Password.
- There's no WordPress at that address: check the address, and in WordPress set **Settings › Permalinks** to anything but **Plain**.
- Application Passwords are turned off: update WordPress, and allow them in your security plugin.
- The site refused the request: a firewall or security plugin is blocking it, so allow it.
- This user can't write posts: use an Author, an Editor or an Administrator.

sections.heading: Connect Framer
sections.text:
In Framer, open the project's **Site Settings › General** and make a key, as a user who can edit the CMS, then copy it. In the **Framer** card, paste the **Project address** as your browser shows it in Framer, and the key, and click **Connect**.

Pick the **Collection** your pages go to, then which field takes the title and the page content and, if you like, the meta title, meta description and structured data. Click **Save**. A collection with a required field GetCito can't fill is marked in the list and can't be saved: make that field optional in Framer first.

sections.heading: Connect Wix
sections.text: The site needs the Wix Blog: pages go there as draft posts. In Wix, the site's owner opens **Account Settings › API Keys Manager**, clicks **Generate API Key**, picks the site, gives the key **Manage Blog** and **Manage Ricos Document**, and copies it; Wix shows it once. In the **Wix** card, paste the **Site id** (or the whole address of the site's dashboard) and the **API key**, and click **Connect**. A Blog with no post can't be connected yet: write one post on it as the site's owner first.

sections.heading: Replace or disconnect
sections.text: Each card has its own way to change the sign-in: **Replace token** for Webflow, **Change sign-in** for WordPress, **Replace key** for Framer and **Change API key** for Wix. **Disconnect** removes the connection; pages already sent stay in your CMS. Framer and Wix don't let GetCito revoke a key, so delete it there too: in the project's **Site Settings › General**, or in Wix's **API Keys Manager**. If the CMS refuses the saved sign-in, the card says so, for example **Sign-in refused** or **Key refused**, and asks for a new one.

sections.heading: Send through your workflow instead
sections.text: Pages can also go to your workflow tool, such as n8n, Make or Zapier, which creates the post in your CMS and decides whether it lands as a draft or goes live. On the **Opportunities** page, open **Webhook Settings**, enter your workflow's address in **Webhook URL**, tick **Content page sent**, which is off by default, and save. Pages you send to **Your workflow** then reach it.

articles.title: Generate a content brief

sections.text: A content brief tells a writer what to write to close an opportunity's gap: the title, the type of content, the outline and the keywords. GetCito writes it with AI from the opportunity's data, in your brand's language. You can then write the page in the Content Editor, or hand the work on to the Action Center or your workflow tool.

sections.heading: Generate a brief
sections.text:
On **Opportunities**, click an opportunity's title. The panel shows its source data and any brief it already has. Admins and managers click **Generate Brief**.

A brief is written once per opportunity: the button then reads **Brief Generated**. Each brief counts toward the month's content briefs, and on plans with monthly limits **This billing period** shows how many are left.

sections.heading: What a brief holds
Write it, or hand it on
sections.text:
- **Send to Editor** opens **New content** with the opportunity picked; the draft starts with the brief's outline and keywords.
- **Send to Actions** puts the work in the Action Center.
- **Send to Workflow** sends it to your workflow tool.

Earned opportunities don't go to the editor: send them to the Action Center or your workflow tool.

sections.heading: A fresh brief in the editor
sections.text: An opportunity's brief is written once and stays as it is. Once the page is in the Content Editor, **Rebuild brief** there writes a new brief from the sources you keep in the draft.

sections.heading: Send it to your workflow
sections.text:
In the opportunity's **…** menu, click **Send to Workflow**. GetCito sends the opportunity, the data behind it and its brief, if it has one, and its status becomes **Sent to Workflow**. The button then reads **Send Again**. To send several at once, tick them on the list and click **Send All**.

The webhook needs **Opportunity sent** ticked. An address that redirects isn't followed, so nothing is sent: use the address it redirects to.

sections.heading: Set up your workflow once
sections.text:
Click **Webhook Settings** at the top of the Opportunities page:

- **Webhook URL**: your workflow tool's address, such as an n8n, Make or Zapier flow, or your own endpoint.
- **Secret Key (optional)**: lets your endpoint tell that a call came from GetCito.
- **Events to send**: **Opportunity sent**, **Daily Pulse created**, **Action Center task sent** and **Content page sent**. A new webhook has the first three ticked; **Content page sent** stays off until you tick it.
- **Active**: turn it off to pause sending without deleting the webhook.

**Test Webhook** always sends a test event. Click **Save Webhook** to keep it. Only admins and managers can change or test the webhook.

sections.heading: After the work is done
sections.text:
Once the opportunity is in the Action Center, its status follows its action: **In Progress** once work starts, **Done** when it's complete. Your workflow tool can also move it on, for example to In Progress or Done.

Admins and managers can also tick opportunities on the list and click **Done**.

articles.title: Write a page in the Content Editor

sections.text: The Content Editor is where pages are written. It opens from the Library, from the Plan, or when you start a page in New content. **Editor** in the sidebar takes you back to the draft you last opened for this brand in this browser; with none, or if that draft was deleted or archived, it opens New content. The page saves as you write.

sections.heading: The header
sections.text:
The header shows the title, which you can click to rename the page, and whether your changes are saved. Under them come the page type, the method and status, a **Rules** chip with how many rules the page meets now (for example **13/15 rules**; click it to open the rules) and the **Quality** score. On a page that optimizes a live one, a chip counts the cited passages kept.

On the right are the month's AI usage and the buttons **History**, **Copy HTML**, **Export**, **Send to CMS** (the paper-plane icon, for admins and managers) and **Mark ready**, and a button to show or hide the side panel.

sections.heading: Site Audit estimate
sections.text:
In the side panel's **Quality**, **Site Audit estimate** (for example **≈62**) is about where the page would score in Site Audit once published, with the score by category: Structure, Content, Authority, Trust and E-E-A-T. It's free, and it's read again each time you pause typing.

It runs Site Audit's checks on the page as it would go out. The checks of your whole site, such as robots.txt, llms.txt and HTTPS, come from your latest Site Audit; with none yet, they're left out.

The 13 checks AI reads aren't in it at first, so it runs a few points under the full audit. **Estimate AI checks** adds them, using a little of your monthly AI usage. They stay in the score as you keep writing; **Read AI checks again** reads them anew.

sections.heading: Status and runs
sections.text: Where your workspace has Chat, a pill next to the title says where the page stands: **Working** while the Content Agent works on it, **Needs you** while its suggestions wait or the page is in review, **Ready**, **Done** once published, or **Draft**. **Runs** at the top lists your own Chat runs and this brand's Content Agent runs, this page's among them; click one to open it. Once the agent's work has started on the server, its card says you can leave the page: it keeps going.

sections.heading: Write and paste
sections.text:
The page starts with its H1, which is also its title. A page has one H1: the toolbar won't add a second one. A paste keeps headings, lists, links and tables, and drops fonts, colors and styles. Press Command or Ctrl + Shift + V to paste plain text.

**Attach a file** inserts Excel, CSV, Word, Markdown, HTML or text, up to 10 MB each; a sheet comes in as a table. **Add HTML** adds an embed, a widget or a form, kept exactly as written; GetCito never runs it. **Edit as HTML** shows the page's source; scripts, iframes and inline styles are removed when you switch back.

sections.heading: Facts and your input
sections.text:
The Content Agent looks up the facts a page needs, such as a price, a plan's limits or a statistic, and links each to the page it came from, never a forum or a social post. A fact no trusted page has is left out of its sentence.

A fact it couldn't look up stays in square brackets for you, as do up to three only your brand has, such as your customer count. Each is tinted amber; **Your input needed** in the toolbar counts them and jumps to the next one, selected so you can type over it.

Ones in alt text, structured data or HTML count too. **Send to CMS** waits until none is left. With Quality on, **Export** offers **Fill now** or **Export without them**, which drops those sentences. One in the title or a heading has to be filled.

sections.heading: Health and supplement brands
sections.text:
The Content Agent never writes a health benefit, a treatment, a prevention or a dose your brand didn't give in its own words, such as that a product helps you sleep or eases stress, and never looks one up. One it wrote anyway is taken out of the page, or its suggestion is dropped. A claim your page, your brand's description or **Your input** already makes can stay, and safety lines such as "talk to your doctor" always do.

A brand counts as a health brand when its industry is Healthcare, or its industry, name or description names supplements, vitamins, a pharmacy, a clinic or wellness.

sections.heading: The side panel
sections.text:
The side panel's tabs are **Instructions**, **Sources** and **Live page**. **Instructions** holds what the Content Agent follows: **Brief** and **Rules**, and **Quality** when it's on, switched at its top. The panel opens on **Instructions**, on **Rules**.

While the panel is closed, its tabs run down the editor's right edge: click one to open the panel there.

Building the brief and running the Content Agent use your workspace's monthly AI usage.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.text:
**Brief** shows the page type, target URL, goal, audience, length, outline and keywords; **Edit brief** changes them. With no brief yet, **Build brief** writes the goal, audience and outline from your sources; once there is one, the button reads **Rebuild brief**. Either writes the outline from the sources you keep, each H2 answering a search AI ran for your prompts. If you edited the brief, rebuilding asks first: **Rebuild anyway** or **Keep my brief**.

A draft started from an opportunity with a brief starts with that brief's outline and keywords.

sections.heading: What the brief reads from cited pages
sections.text:
Building the brief also reads a few of the pages AI cited. Their typical length shows beside **Length**, and **Cited pages have** lists what Site Audit's checks find on at least half of them, such as an FAQ schema, tables or statistics. The Content Agent then writes the page toward what its text can carry, not its schema, dates or byline, which your site sets.

Once the brief has an outline, **Rewrite from brief**, for a new page, or **Suggest changes from brief**, for an existing one, hands the page to the Content Agent. The page you have now stays in History.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text:
**Sources** shows what the draft is built from: **Prompts**, **Fan-outs** (the searches AI ran for your prompts), **Cited pages**, which AI quotes today, and **Search Console** queries. Each source shows where the draft uses it.

Uncheck a source to leave it out, or click **Add source** to add a prompt, a page address or a Search Console query. Then click **Rebuild with selection**.

sections.heading: Live page
sections.text:
For a draft that optimizes a live page, **Live page** shows how that page does now: **Citations**, **AI visits**, **Google clicks** and **Prompts cited**, over 7 days to a year, against the period before. It is not a forecast of what the draft will get.

- Prompts that stopped citing the page are marked **Lost**. **Use the lost prompts in this draft** adds them to the sources and rebuilds the brief.
- **Results from AI visits** shows the AI visits that landed on the page and, with Google Analytics connected, their key events, orders and revenue, by AI source.
- **Your other pages for these prompts** lists your other pages cited for the same prompts.
- With conversions from AI visits on, **Conversions from AI journeys** shows what the journeys through the page brought in.

A new page has nothing to measure until it's marked published with its live address.

sections.heading: Passages AI cites are locked
sections.text: When a draft optimizes a live page brought in by its URL, the passages AI answers quoted in the last 30 days are marked in green, and a chip in the header counts them. The Content Agent never changes these passages. If you edit one, the editor asks first: **Keep wording** or **Edit anyway**. Changing a quoted passage may cost the page those citations.

sections.heading: History, Copy HTML and Export
sections.text:
- **History** keeps earlier versions for 90 days: the live page as imported, the page before agent changes, each Mark ready and publish, each Hand off, and the page before a restore. **Restore** makes a new version, so nothing is lost.
- **Copy HTML** copies the whole page as HTML, HTML blocks and schema included, to paste into your CMS. An article also gets the Article schema GetCito adds, with its author.
- **Export** downloads the page as **Word**, **Excel**, **CSV**, **HTML** or **Markdown**. Excel and CSV hold the page as one row, for a CMS's import. Only the HTML file carries the schema.

With Quality on, **Export** opens a dialog instead: the same files, and under **Platforms** a copy of the page to paste into Webflow, WordPress, Shopify or Google Docs.

sections.heading: Add products from your catalog
sections.text: On an online shop's draft, **Products** in the toolbar adds products from your catalog: search by name, pick one to four that are in stock, and click **Insert**. One shows as a card, more as a grid, each with its picture, name and price, linked to its page. A card keeps its price: to show today's, delete the card and add the product again.

sections.heading: Mark ready
sections.text:
**Mark ready** saves the page, sets it to **Ready** and keeps a version in History. If the draft was sent to the Action Center, it also completes its task there. With Quality on, **Mark ready** opens **Before you publish** first.

GetCito doesn't publish the page: copy or export it to your site, or send it to your CMS.

Click **Ready** in the header to move the page back to **In review**. A task that Mark ready completed is open again, unless someone changed it in the Action Center since or the action is closed.

sections.heading: Mark published
sections.text:
Once the page is live, tell GetCito where with **Mark published**, in the Library's **Status** menu or, with Quality on, under the header's **Next step** once the page is ready. It asks for the live address, starting from the page it optimizes or your site with the page's slug, and **Live page** measures that address from then. If the draft came from the Action Center, its Publish task is completed once all the action's work is live.

On a published page, the header's **Published** button changes the address. A page your CMS reports live, or one published in Webflow, WordPress, Framer or Wix, gets its address on its own. Restore an archived page in the Library first.

articles.title: Manage drafts in the Content Library

sections.text: The **Library**, under **Content** in the sidebar, lists every page you, your teammates and the Content Agent wrote or changed in GetCito. Click a row to open the draft in the editor.

sections.heading: The tabs
sections.text:
Each tab shows its count:

- **All**: every draft that isn't archived.
- **In progress**: drafts being written.
- **In review**: drafts the Content Agent wrote, waiting for a person.
- **Ready**: drafts marked ready.
- **Published**: drafts marked published, by you or your CMS.
- **Archived**: drafts sent to the archive. They keep their status for when they're restored.

sections.heading: Columns and filters
sections.text: The columns are Content, Type, Method (Create or Optimize), By (you, the Content Agent or a teammate), Made in (Content Editor, Chat, Action Center, Agent or MCP), Status, Created and Updated. A draft made in your own chat has **Open chat**, and the editor shows **From chat** with its title. While the Content Agent writes a draft, its Status reads **Agent writing…**, and **Agent failed** if it couldn't finish; where your workspace has Chat, each comes with the same dot Chat shows for a run. The **Created** filter narrows the list to the last 7, 30 or 90 days, and **Made in** to one place, once drafts come from more than one. Once a page has been sent to your CMS, the **Last send** filter lists the pages by how their last send went: never sent, sending, sent, failed or published.

sections.heading: The row menu
sections.text:
- **Status**: set the draft to In progress, In review, Ready or Published. Ready works like the editor's Mark ready, and Published, not offered for archived drafts, asks for the page's live address. Moving a ready or published draft back to In progress or In review opens its task again. A published one also opens the action's Publish task again and stops its Live page being measured for the action.
- **Export Word**, **Export Excel**, **Export CSV**, **Export HTML** or **Export Markdown** for that draft.
- **Send to CMS**: send the draft to your CMS, except an archived one. Admins and managers can tick several rows to send up to 25 at once.
- **Send to Archive** or **Restore**.
- **Delete**: the draft leaves the Library for good, with its versions and suggestions. An Action Center task it was sent as stays.

Send to CMS, archiving and deleting are for admins and managers.

sections.heading: Export the list
sections.text:
**Export** in the header downloads the drafts listed, that is the current tab within the **Created** range and the **Last send** filter:

- **Export CSV** and **Export Excel**: one row per draft, with its title, status, method, page type, author, dates, page address, length and text.
- **Export Word**: one document, each draft starting on a page of its own.

sections.heading: Shopping path check for online shops
sections.text:
For an online shop, the **Shopping path** column shows what the last check found for each draft with a shopping path. After each catalog sync, every such draft is read again. A draft needs attention when it links a product that is sold out, refused by Merchant Center or gone from your catalog; hover the mark to see the products. The **Shopping path** filter lists the drafts that need attention, are fine, or have none.

When a published page links a product that no longer sells, a **Fix** action opens in the Action Center, and **Swap in the editor** opens the draft.

articles.title: Find content opportunities

sections.text: The **Opportunities** page, under **Content** in the sidebar, lists content opportunities: what to write or change so AI answers name you where they don't yet. GetCito suggests them on its own as tracking data comes in. An opportunity is built for a group of related prompts that one piece of content can answer, or for a single prompt. From each one you can start writing, plan it, brief it or send it on.

sections.heading: What each row shows
Filter, sort and export
sections.text:
- Search the opportunities, and narrow the list by topic, prompt, type, impact, **Source** and status. The sources are **System**, suggested automatically; **Manual**, made with **New**; **Prompt**, suggested from a prompt; and **Action**, sent from an Action Center task.
- **Suggested** picks a period, all time, this month, the last 30 days or your own dates, and the order: highest score, newest or oldest.
- Archived opportunities stay hidden unless you filter to them.
- Most filters and the order stay in the page's address, so a link opens the same view; the topic and the search don't.
- **Export CSV** downloads every opportunity that matches the filters and the search, not only the page you see.

sections.heading: Quick actions on a row
Work on many at once
sections.text:
Tick rows, or the box in the header for every row shown, then:

- **Send All** sends each one to your workflow tool, which suits kicking off a content sprint.
- **Done**, **Dismiss All** and **Delete** change them all at once. They're for admins and managers.

**Delete** removes the opportunities for good, with any brief they have, and doesn't give back the month's opportunities or briefs. Dismissing keeps them out of your way instead.

sections.heading: Ask for new opportunities
sections.text:
Admins and managers click **New** to get suggestions now, instead of waiting for the next automatic run. Pick a **Focus**: **Let GetCito choose**, a **Topic** or a **Prompt**. You can add your own idea, up to 500 characters, and set **How many**. New opportunities also follow the brand's rules from **Settings › Content › Brand rules**, such as topics to stay away from.

Opportunities are written per group of prompts: prompts of one topic that a single page could answer, and that already have tracked answers. Each group gets one opportunity; only **Another angle** adds a second take on it.

Titles leave years out unless the need is about one. A year that has passed in an opportunity's title or question shows as this year; your tracked prompts keep their own words.

sections.heading: What each focus picks
sections.text:
- **Let GetCito choose** takes the highest-scoring groups that have no opportunity yet, one from each topic first.
- **Topic** takes only that topic's groups. Each topic in the list shows how many new groups it has, or **All covered**.
- **Prompt** takes only that prompt's group, so it writes at most one opportunity, and **How many** stays at 1. If the group already has an open opportunity, the dialog says so and offers **Open existing** instead; prompts like that show **Has one** in the list. A prompt whose opportunity was dismissed or done can be asked for again.

sections.heading: How many are left
sections.text: The dialog shows how many groups in your focus have no opportunity yet, and **How many** goes no higher. When none are left, it says so and **Generate** stays off: add prompts for new groups, or use **Another angle** on an opportunity. Groups without tracked answers from the last 30 days have nothing to write from yet.

sections.heading: No duplicates
sections.text:
GetCito never writes the same work twice. When a new opportunity would cover the same need as one you have, because their prompts and AI searches largely overlap, it's added to that one instead and skipped. If nothing new is written, the message says so and counts any duplicates it skipped.

A question also gets only one open opportunity. When a new one would answer the same question as an open one, in the same words (years aside) or from the same group of prompts, it's added to the open one. That holds for automatic suggestions, **New**, a prompt's suggestion and a task sent from the Action Center. Its prompts, AI searches and sources join the open one, which keeps the stronger score and counts what was added. The task's History says where it went.

For a second take on the same need, use **Another angle** on the opportunity.

sections.heading: How many you get
sections.text: New opportunities come from a monthly allowance set by your plan, with a cap on how many one request asks for; on limited plans the page shows what's left. Skipped duplicates and opportunities that couldn't be written don't count; **Another angle** counts as one new opportunity. The up to three new opportunities GetCito writes by itself each night come from the same allowance.

sections.heading: Owned and earned
sections.text:
Each opportunity has a **Type**. **Owned** means content on your own site. **Earned** means coverage on other sites, such as articles, reviews and links. Some gaps are best closed with a guest post or a press placement rather than a new page of your own.

Earned opportunities don't go to the Content Editor: send them to the Action Center or your workflow tool.

sections.heading: Pick what to work on
sections.text: Don't ship every brief. Editorial time is usually the bottleneck, so pick the two to four high-impact opportunities a week your team can really write, and leave the rest for later.

articles.title: Use the Content plan

sections.text: The **Content plan**, **Plan** under **Content** in the sidebar, ranks what to create, optimize or protect next. It covers the last 7, 30 or 90 days: pick the period at the top right.

sections.heading: The four cards
sections.text:
- **Create**: new pages AI needs, that is open opportunities with no page on your site yet.
- **Optimize**: pages losing ground, and opportunities to improve a page you already have.
- **Protect**: your top pages, cited at least five times in the period and not losing ground, up to five, and opportunities to defend a page.
- **Priority**: rows your team marked as a priority.

Click a card to filter the list to it, and click it again to clear the filter.

sections.heading: When a page is losing ground
sections.text: A page is losing ground when it is cited at least 20% less per tracked answer than in the period before, from at least three citations. Because the comparison is per tracked answer, a week with fewer runs, or prompts added or removed, doesn't move a page. If tracking began during the earlier period, a note above the list says so.

sections.heading: The priority list
sections.text:
Each row shows the **Priority Score**; the **Page**, with its title, page type and path, or **New page**; the **Action**: Create, Optimize or Protect; **Why** it's listed, tagged with where that comes from (**Opportunity**, **Citations** or **Protect**); and **Who** is on it: you, the Agent, a teammate or the person it's assigned to.

The row's button, **Create**, **Optimize** or **View**, opens New content on that row, and **Open draft** opens the draft already being written. Rows marked as a priority come first, the rest by score. The list shows up to 50 rows.

sections.heading: How the Priority Score works
sections.text:
The score runs from 0 to 100 and is built from four factors:

- **Severity**: how urgent the row is. A page losing citations counts most, then a new page AI needs, a page to improve and a page to protect.
- **Opportunity**: the score of the content opportunity behind the row.
- **Page value**: the page's AI visits and, with conversions on, the conversions from AI journeys through it.
- **Citations**: how often AI answers cited the page.

A row without an opportunity, a new page, or a brand with no AI traffic data counts as neutral, not zero. Hover the score to see **How this score is worked out**. Only a page losing citations can reach critical.

sections.heading: The row menu
sections.text:
- **Assign to…**: for a row with a draft, pick a teammate and the draft goes to the Action Center as their task. For a row without one, New content opens with **Team** chosen.
- **Mark as priority** or **Remove priority**: the row moves to the top of the list, tagged **Priority**. **Send to Plan** on an opportunity does the same.
- **Hide from the plan**: the row leaves the list and the counts. Undo it from the message that appears, or later from the hidden rows under the list, with **Show again**.

Only admins and managers can mark priorities and hide rows.

sections.heading: What AI cites in your topics
sections.text:
A line above the list shows what visitors from AI assistants did on your site in the period: visits and, with Google Analytics connected, key events, orders and revenue.

Under **What AI cites in your topics**, click **Show**. For each page type, it compares the share of AI citations that go to that type with its share of your own cited pages. A type AI cites 10 points or more beyond your own mix is marked as a **Gap**. Click a row to filter the priority list to that page type; click it again, or **Clear**, to remove the filter. The page types follow your brand's **Site type** in the brand settings.

sections.heading: Shopping opportunities
sections.text:
For an online shop whose product catalog, in **Settings › Integrations**, has categories, **Shopping opportunities** above the list shows two kinds of rows:

- **Buying guide · New**: a category with at least three products in stock that no page of yours guides shoppers to yet. **Create** starts a buying guide draft and opens it in the editor.
- **Existing post · Fix**: a published post that links a product that no longer sells, or misses some of its category pages. **Optimize** opens it in the editor.

articles.title: Write to the Content Editor rules
synonyms: let the agent fix the page

sections.text: Every page in the Content Editor is written to a set of rules for its page type. The **Rules** chip in the header shows how many the page meets now; click it to open the rules. **Fix open rules** asks the Content Agent to suggest changes for the rules the page doesn't meet yet; **Rewrite page** rewrites the whole page to them.

sections.heading: The Rules tab
sections.text: In the side panel, **Instructions** opens on **Rules**. The rules come in five groups: page type rules, length and structure, fan-outs and keywords, links and sources, and style. Most rules can be turned on or off, and many have a value you can change. Each rule's status is read from the page as you write. Rules marked **AI check** are judged by the Content Agent and aren't counted yet.

sections.heading: Save or reset your rules
sections.text: Changes to the rules apply to this draft only. **Save as my rules**, for admins and managers, keeps them for your workspace's next drafts of this page type, and **Reset** goes back to the default set. Under **Your text rules**, write a rule in your own words, or use **Paste many** to add several from a style guide.

sections.heading: Brand rules
sections.text: Admins and managers keep a brand's rules in **Settings › Content › Brand rules**, one per line, up to 30, such as topics to stay away from. The Content Agent follows them on every page of the brand, before your text rules, and a brand rule wins when they disagree. They change what's written, not the **Rules** count.

sections.heading: Fix open rules
sections.text:
**Fix open rules** sits at the top of **Rules**. It asks the Content Agent to suggest small, reviewable changes for the rules the page doesn't meet yet. Its suggestions appear in the page, each with **Accept** and **Reject**, under a bar with **Accept all** and **Reject all**.

A decided suggestion can be taken back with **Undo** or **Restore**, and **Undo all** brings every one back to review. One run makes at most eight changes: run it again for the rules still open. Running the agent uses your workspace's monthly AI usage.

An open rule shows its status in amber; red is kept for what blocks. Once you've decided a run's suggestions, a rule it tried and couldn't fix gets an amber label and a note that it's yours to decide: change the page yourself, or the rule.

sections.heading: Rewrite the whole page
sections.text:
The **▾** menu beside **Fix open rules** also offers **Rewrite the whole page**: one new version written to every rule, with the cited passages kept. It uses more AI usage than fixing open rules. It's marked **Recommended** when the page is far off its Length or many rules are open. Picked, the button reads **Rewrite page**.

A rewrite comes back as one change: **Compare** it with your page, then **Accept** or **Reject**. Your page before it stays in History. A rewrite isn't offered once the page is ready or published. One past its Length is cut to it with one more pass; accept one still a little long, and the next rewrite starts from there.

When the passages it keeps stop the page reaching its Length, a note offers **Raise Length to …** and **Rewrite, cited passages too**, which may stop those passages being quoted. The **Length** rule says so too.

sections.heading: Before you run it again
sections.text:
- Accept or reject the open suggestions before you run the agent again or edit the page as HTML.
- The agent doesn't change heading levels: turn extra H1s into H2s in the toolbar yourself.
- The agent only changes drafts, not published pages.

sections.heading: How your choices teach the agent
sections.text: What you accept and reject teaches the agent. For a rule whose suggestions this brand has mostly rejected over the last 90 days (at least five decided, on two pages or more, seven in ten rejected), it keeps its changes as small as the rule allows, and its card says which rules while it works. Only its small changes count: a rejected **Rewrite the whole page** doesn't. Quality's **Hand off** isn't affected.

sections.heading: On a page that is already live
sections.text: When the draft optimizes a live page, the agent is also told how that page does now, as the **Live page** tab shows it over 30 days: how often AI answers cite it and the prompts it lost. It keeps the answers and facts AI engines cite, answers a lost prompt's question where a rule's change can, and its card says what it kept in mind.

articles.title: Open an opportunity and act on it

sections.text: On **Opportunities**, click an opportunity's title to open it in a panel beside the list. The page's address keeps it, so a link opens it too. **Open in new tab**, in the row's **…** menu, opens it as a page of its own. The panel shows what the opportunity rests on, and every action you can take on it.

sections.heading: What it rests on
sections.text:
**Source Data** shows the related prompt, **Est. AI Volume**, your **Current Visibility**, the **Competitor Gap**, the **Strongest Competitor**, the **Search Intent**, the keywords, the searches AI engines ran for the prompt, and the competitors cited.

An opportunity sent from an Action Center task shows that task instead: where, why, how, and when it's done.

**Results** lists the Action Center actions sent from the opportunity, with what changed once their work is complete and measured.

sections.heading: For a group of prompts
sections.text:
An opportunity built for a group of prompts also shows:

- **Your Site**: which of your pages to work on, with their AI citations and sessions over 30 days.
- **Recommended Assets**: the main piece of work and any supporting ones. Each can go to the Action Center on its own.
- **Opportunity Basket**: its prompts, and the searches AI engines ran for them.
- **Why This Score**: demand counts 40%, the visibility gap 30%, the competitor gap 20% and intent 10%, measured over the last 30 days.

sections.heading: The panel's buttons
sections.text:
- **Send to Actions** makes the opportunity an action in the Action Center. The button then reads **Open in Actions**.
- **Generate Brief** writes a content brief. It's for admins and managers, and once the brief is written the button reads **Brief Generated**.
- **Send to Editor** opens **New content** with the opportunity picked: a new page, or the page of yours it names to optimize. Once a draft is being written for it, the button reads **Open draft**. It's offered for owned opportunities that are still open.
- **Write this**, beside it, has the Content Agent brief and write the page in one go. See below.
- **Export** downloads the opportunity as CSV, Excel or Word.

sections.heading: Write this
sections.text:
**Write this**, on the panel and in a row's **…** menu, takes an owned opportunity to a page to review in one go. First it says what will happen and about how much of your monthly AI usage it takes. Then:

1. The Content Agent builds a brief from the opportunity's prompts, their fan-outs and the pages AI cites for them.
2. It writes the page from the brief, by your rules and the page type's. For an opportunity on a page you have, it suggests changes to that page instead.
3. The editor opens and shows the agent at work. You review the page there, with a free estimate of its Site Audit score; nothing is published.

You can stop it from the editor. If the brief can't be built, the agent writes from what there is.

sections.heading: The … menu
sections.text:
The panel's **…** menu holds the rest:

- **Send to Plan**, for admins and managers: the opportunity goes to the top of the Content plan. Once it's a priority there, it reads **Open in Plan**.
- **Another angle**, except on an opportunity sent from the Action Center.
- **Send to Workflow**, which reads **Send Again** once it's sent.
- **Copy All Data**.
- **Mark as reviewed**, for a new opportunity: its status becomes Reviewed.
- **Restore**, for an archived one: it comes back as New.
- **Dismiss**.

sections.heading: Another angle
sections.text:
**Another angle**, for admins and managers, writes one more opportunity for the same need, with a different content type, format, audience or approach. You can add a direction of your own. Both opportunities stay in the list, so you keep the one you prefer.

It counts as one of the month's new opportunities.

sections.heading: Dismiss an opportunity
sections.text:
**Dismiss**, for admins and managers, asks why:

- **The topic doesn't matter to us** keeps it from being suggested again in this form for 90 days.
- **Right topic, wrong angle** dismisses it and opens **Another angle**, so you can ask for a better take on the same need.

sections.heading: Follow it to Done
sections.text:
Once an opportunity is in the Action Center, its status follows its action: **In Progress** once work on it starts, **Done** when it's complete. Its **Results** card shows what changed once the work has been measured.

A done opportunity comes back as **New**, marked **New signal detected**, when its score has risen since, or the visibility its work gained didn't hold.

articles.title: Check a page's Quality in the Content Editor

sections.text: Quality scores a Content Editor page and lists what would raise it. It's turned on per installation: where it's off, nothing on this page shows. With it on, **Instructions** in the side panel has a third segment, **Quality**, and the header a **Quality** chip with the page's score.

sections.heading: The scores
sections.text:
Quality scores the page from 0 to 100 on three things, each card saying what it scores:

- **E-E-A-T**: who stands behind the page, such as its author and their experience.
- **Trust**: sources, links and dated facts.
- **Readability**: how easily it reads.

80 and up is **Strong**, 60 to 79 **Can improve**, and under 60 **Needs work**. The header's **Quality** chip is the average of the three. The scores are GetCito's estimates from Google's published quality signals, not a Google score.

Under them, **Site Audit estimate** is about where the page would score in Site Audit. See the Content Editor article.

At the bottom, **Site trust**, out of 5, comes from Site Audit's checks of your site, with **Fix in Site Audit** when some are missing.
